text: The Wild Beaver Saloon is one of those places in Nashville that really gets overlooked...or the name just freaks you out. Okay, okay--I am not going to lie. It freaked me out. I mean, a BEAVER? WILD BEAVER? Maybe 26 is old, but I remember the days and what the slang of beaver represented! I was not going to a bar that basically read Wild Pussy. Sorry. It wasn't like I would never go, it was just one of those things I wasn't going to make a special trip out to that one location! It scared me! But when I ended up there, I was pleasantly surprised and the Beaver logo they have is, well um...tactfully cute! When I went in there, there was an electronic bull in the middle of the entire place - it was one of those transportable ones, but it was pretty cool - it took up a lot of space and seems to be one of those things that gets more attention, the drunker you get. Now don't get me wrong: I would have loved to have rode the bull, but literally, you are in the middle of the entire place and there probably wasn't enough vodka on Broadway to get my beaver on that bull...no pun intended! It's one of those things that you might not want everyone to see you grasping on while the electronic bull, controlled by a guy you can clearly see on the side, controls your fate with a flick of his wrist and a snickering grin..you are literally the entertainment if you are on the bull and the bull seemed to have a dirty mind all on its own! The prices are average and the service is good - everyone was friendly when they came around. I like bars where there is room and the entire bar is very open. I love playing corn hole - I went on a date and was able to talk to my husband as well, which is always something I find worth noting, especially when you are in Honkey Tonk land! Overall, it is a very FUN place and somewhere cool to go and don't let the name freak you out - the beaver is actually quite cute!
label: POS

text: Oh my. Oh ho ho ho ho my. This is some darn good BBQ. I took the day off last Friday, and I wanted to treat myself to a delicious lunch. I needed to head downtown for some errands, and Bogart's was in the neighborhood. I had been wanting to try it for quite some time, and I figured that would be a good day to try it. I stood in line for about 10 minutes, which gave me time to study the menu and decide what I wanted to get. I heard about the similarities between Pappy's (which I LOVE) and Bogart's, so I knew whatever I ordered was bound to be delicious. I settled with a half rack of ribs, baked beans, and cole slaw. It was a beautiful day, so I sat at one of the tables outside. They had a few tables indoors, but those were all full. Similar to Pappy's, just when I needed a table, one opened up. So outside I went. The food came out pretty quickly, and it all looked delicious. I started with the baked beans. AMAZING. Smoky, a little spicy, and piping hot. I loved these. The cole slaw was equally tasty. It was mayonnaise based, I believe, which gave it a rich creaminess that I adored. SO tasty! On to the main event: the ribs. The meat on these ribs literally fell off the bone, making them extremely easy to eat. I tried a bit of all four sauces Bogart's offered, but I fell in love with their Voodoo Sauce (the spicy one -- of course!). There were a few employees making the rounds to all of the tables to ensure everyone's meals were fine. I gave them the thumbs up, dirty fingers, face, and all. This stuff was GOOD. Unlike Pappy's, Bogart's didn't have a line that wrapped around the block, which was a good thing. However, since I visited on a Friday afternoon, I probably didn't get a true sense of how crowded it could get. In any event, I loved it, and I will DEFINITELY be back! Bogart's and Pappy's in the same city? We St. Louisans sure are lucky!
label: POS

text: I have eaten at Crabby Larry's several times and the food and service was always great......until my most recent visit. I ordered the rainbow trout stuffed with crab imperial. Now I understand that anytime you order fish, an OCCASIONAL bone may show up in the fish. However, there wasn't a part of this fish that didn't have bone in it. And no where on the menu did it say all bones left in this fish. Every bite, no matter from what portion was a mouthful of bones, at leat 10 large bones. It was totally inedible. I sent it back and they took it off the bill. The waiter was pleasent and I was just going to chalk it up to a mistake. No big deal, wasn't going to change my opinion about Crabby Larry's. However, the waiter then came back and proceeded to lecture me by saying, "I'm not trying to blame you, but this fish does have the spine left in and you have to eat away from the spine." As if I have never eaten a piece of fish in my life. This fish did not have the spine left in, it had every possible bone the fish was born with left in. I was understanding up until that point. That was a horrible thing to do. You don't come back to the table and blame the customer. I'm not sure if that direction came from the cook or "Crabby Larry" himself, but it was enough to make me never go back there again.

text: I enjoy beer very much, therefore, I love 1702! Mucho beer on tap + delicious pizza = a VERY happy me! Visited last night for my bf's family get together and it was packed (as usual). We were able to snag a table after waiting for 15 mins. I've only ever had beer at 1702 but was really excited to try the pizza because it always looks so good! To start we ordered the Hop bread and wings. OMG the Hop bread was amazing. It was covered in cheese and garlic and had a hoppy bitter taste that went so well with the warm marinara. The wings were okay. The hot sauce was standard and tasty but the wings were a little soggy....I am not a fan of wiggly chicken skin. I like that were not fried but the skin kinda freaked me out. Aside from wiggly skin the chicken was tender and overall tasty. After we nommed all that, we placed our pizza order: 14" Islanda, hold the Green peppers and a 14" Pepperoni. The Islanda was amazing. I loves LOVES me some cheese and the Islanda was covered is slightly melted Feta...I mean COVERED! mmmm The pepperoni was a standard pepperoni pizza, lots of pepperoni but not too much. The crusts were very crispy on the bottom and soft on top. I can't wait to go back and get their calzone. As far as beer went, my original choice was the Velvet Merlin (Merkin) because after our 10 day long beer and wine tour, the Velvet Merlin was the beer I absolutely fell in love with and it's sold at Total Wine! Just my luck they were all out. The waitress was nice enough to bring a few samples of other similar beers w/o wasting time. I didn't like either so I ordered the Milk stout. That beer is like a meal, very rich and heavy and head is like melted ice cream. I love it. After that I ordered a floral IPA to go along with the pizza. I forget the name but it was good, not something I'd get to casually sip but it did go very well with the Islanda. This be one of my fave places to drink beer!

text: I have been to this mall probably a million times. When I was young I would spend Saturdays or Sundays here with my dad and I remember just being amazed at the sheer size of it. I once got lost here and grabbed a mans hand, thinking he was my dad, and being so embarrassed to see he was a complete stranger. Anyway, they definitely have a lot of great stores here. I was on a mission to find a few things, and I pretty much knew spending a day here would be a success. For some reason it doesn't seem as big to me anymore, but maybe that's because I've been here so many times that I know it like the back of my hand. Parking wasn't as bad as I thought it would be, we actually scored a spot about 15 meters away from the door, perfect timing I guess. I had to peek into the waterpark and at the sea lions - just for old times sake. I like the waterpark but its way too expensive and I kind of feel sorry for the sea lions. It is pretty cool to think about those things being in a mall though. I didn't get a chance to walk through Galaxyland, which is always fun. They do have a lot of duplicate stores here but I don't mind, and its nice to see some of the old stores are still hanging around. We checked out T&T, crazy busy, but got some good cheap sushi for lunch. Bourbon Street had a bunch of new restaurants that look promising, and of course good ol' Hooters (which evidently, you don't need to have anymore to work there). You can definitely see the malls age now, its starting to look dated, although I LOVE the new fountains/sitting areas as they look very fresh and modern. The mall seems brighter and cleaner as well. A little sad that the big whale is gone, many memories of that, although it did smell really bad and to be honest, it was pretty ugly. Of course I love the new additions, like Anthropologie, Pinkberry, etc. I enjoy coming here on the occasions I'm in Edmonton if I have a whole day to walk around and browse. But I would never come here if I just needed one thing or to get in and out quickly - that would be a nightmare!

Wife had the seared rare ahi-tuna salad with mixed greens and a delicious soy/ginger dressing. Mom-mom had the scallop special which were perfectly seared large diver scallops, balsamic reduction with sautéed vegetables; really nice. I should mention that the scallops were cooked perfectly, not overdone like many restaurants have a tendency to do. The kids had a burger, chicken and french dip sandwiches which were all solid if nothing special. I can say the burger was cooked perfectly medium as requested. The accompanying french fries were excellent (and a great match with my Belgian style beer)! Deserts were good but nothing special. Chocolate peanut butter cake, cheesecake, etc, probably made elsewhere and shipped in but all tasty nonetheless. I was reluctant at first but pleasantly surprised by my experience at Timber Grill. text: On a visit to Indy, cousin-in-law and wife took me, the mrs., and sis-in-law to this tiny hole-in-the-wall DIVE--didn't look like much, but man, appearances do deceive! We went on a Monday night, which was a bonus, because Sean was at the piano banging out standards, and then it was sing-along and karaoke, and we had a blast! On the down side (the reason for not making 5 stars) it was a hot summer night in July, and the A/C just wasn't up to the job, so we were uncomfortably warm. My shirt was soaking wet by the time we left. But the food is out of this world good. When I say this place is tiny, I mean, in the non-smoking area where we were sitting, there couldn't have been room for more than 25 people. So if we hadn't been so lucky with our timing, arriving as they were clearing a table, and just before some other folks got there, we might have had a long wait. Be aware this place will fill up fast. Now to the food and beverage: no beers on draft, but a large selection of bottled beers, so you can get what you like. A full-service bar, if you want mixed drinks, with different specials nightly. A variety of wines, if that's your thing. I ordered grilled grouper with mac n cheese, and they kindly let me sub grilled veggies for the house salad. The veggies were perfectly done, just slightly al dente--for me it could not have been better. The fish was fantastic, great flavor, I could have used tartar sauce, but the fish had enough flavor that t.s. was not necessary. The mac n cheese very creamy, and again perfect flavoring. Cuz-in-law went for the ham sandwich, said it was wonderful. The ladies all had meat w salad combos: one w steak skewer, two with grilled tuna steak. All gave high praise to their plates, and I also got to sample both the tuna and steak; very savory! Save room for dessert! The coconut cream pie is everything other reviewers have said. I had a butterscotch cream pie: absolutely to DIE for. We get back to Indy to visit fam every summer. We will definitely go back to Ralphs, probably a Monday night for the pianoke. We visit Indy most every summer to see family. We will for sure go back to Ralphs, probably on a Monday for the pianoke!

Overall the portions were generous. I didn't finish the pasta and I can pack away some noodles trust me. Each entree was under $20/person - some might be higher like the steak but it's very reasonably priced overall. Especially for the high quality of the food. Jane was the perfect place for a dinner with mom but I would not hesitate to take anyone there. I think all kinds of people would enjoy dining here.

text: I came here for dinner last night with the BF. It was his treat for my birthday, and boy, what a treat. This intimate BYO off a busy Center City street serves delicious, locally sourced food from a menu that rotates weekly. The food is fresh and perfectly seasoned, the staff is friendly and warm, and the ambiance is terrific. Definitely one of Philly's best kept secrets and a memorable dining experience. We started with the White Bean Sformato and the Mortadella and Fig Ravioli. His appetizer (the sformato) was creamy and delicious, especially with the smoked trout. I didn't enjoy the greens, but they were still very crisp. My ravioli was great: a little sweet, a little savory, and a great balance of flavor for the filling. My main course, the Pan Roasted Hen with Carmelized Squash was unlike anything else I've ever had. I rarely have chicken when I dine out, but this was among some of the best I've eaten. The skin was crispy, the meat was juicy and flavorful, and the sides were savory and slightly salty. It provided a great balance of flavor to the dish. His veal leg with polenta and string beans was also terrific. Dessert didn't disappoint either. My ice cream sandwich with brown butter ice cream, nectarines, and shortbread was nothing short of amazing and one of the best desserts I've had (even without chocolate!). Creamy, not overly sweet, and a robust mix of spices with sweetness. Absolutely excellent. I'm excited to come back here another time when the menu changes and I can try more of the great food that Russet puts out. Not only does it taste great, but it's beautifully presented and artfully crafted. It's also greatly enhanced by the friendly, warm, and attentive staff and the charming intimate decor and atmosphere that truly makes any night special. I highly recommend Russet for a change of pace from the Garces and Starr restaurants.

text: I've been to Bricktops twice. Many other reviews are better-informed than mine, so in contrast to my usual loquacious style, I'm going to keep this baby pretty short and sweet. First, you must try the BBQ chicken flatbread. I'm not usually one for BBQ chicken pizzas, but the flavors and preparation of Bricktops are simply wonderful. It's got peanuts on it, which in my opinion really "make" the dish. If you're a spice hound like me, they can also bring you a bottle of Melinda's Habanero sauce to go with it. Heaven. Second, if it's a nice day, I highly endorse a late Sunday brunch in the outside seating. The ambience is pleasant, and you're just close enough to West End to watch, without being so close that you feel like you're caught in traffic. Plus, you can get a carafe of their house champagne for $20, and in the context of the rest of the menu prices, that's a borderline steal. As for entrees, my experience is pretty limited. I tried the halibut for dinner one time, which I thought was pretty awesome. At my last visit (the brunch), I ordered the bleu cheese burger, which was pretty tasty too -- although at $12 for a burger, it ought to be! If I were to pick on something, it would be the crab cake salad. It wasn't bad or anything -- it just didn't merit its $18 price tag. Overall, Bricktops is a pretty cool place with some unique menu items, if you can stomach the bill.

text: I arrived here with a friend wanting to experience upscale dining. Reviews were good. Great! Let's go! (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/buddakan-philadelphia?select=emKANtA7xx8JdasuUWFSvg#vBhLseDzPPr7mPleLMx7cw).Seating not available. The hosts were very amicable and apologetic. Very nice smile, though. I wonder if this restaurant only hires beautiful people, because ever waiter/host looks as if they belonged to some fashion magazine. Asks if it is our first time at this restaurant. It is! Great! Gives a 5 minute introduction about Buddhakan and why it's unique (it's because the food is more oriented towards sharing than individual entrees) 9:50 - Jennifer comes by and offers her apologies for our long wait. Gives us a complimentary Edamame Ravioli(http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/buddakan-philadelphia?select=emKANtA7xx8JdasuUWFSvg#emKANtA7xx8JdasuUWFSvg). Aweeesome! Came with three pieces... I was hoping this wouldn't be indicative of the portions of the other dishes. Was pretty good, though. The consistency inside the ravioli was as good as can be. Friend and I also decided to order after Jennifer stops by a couple times. Asks us if we want Fiji water, sparkling water, or ice water. Ignorant on my part, I thought this was complimentary. Apparently not. My fault. 10:00- Friend and I decided to order one restaurant week course for the both of us, including a couple extra desserts. After telling Jennifer, her face freezes for a moment, and recaptures her composure after a second. *Did I say something wrong?*. "Absolutely!" That was the last word I heard from her. I don't know why she stopped talking to us, but maybe she found out my friend and I are simply commoners and would maybe not be able to afford a separate course for each person? Maybe we wouldn't be able to give as large a tip as we would otherwise? I mean... the food is meant to be shared, so why not share, right? What happened to the lovely facade she was putting up? She just stop talking to us. No you're welcome after she poured us our water. As in... nothing. I was a bit offended. I was NOT expecting such a change in demeanor. Bleh. 10:10 Our first entree comes! Char Siu Bun!(http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/buddakan-philadelphia?select=emKANtA7xx8JdasuUWFSvg#NAM0pPswlpxsOendP1j8hg) I know what good Chinese food tastes like, and this was NOTHING like good Chinese food. For $12, we got two buns of Char Siu, that barely had any pork in the filling. The pork was also not sweet as it should be. The one thing that was different from normal Char Siu was the the outside was a bit fried. Good touch, but the bread wasn't chewy or soft. The pork was warm, not hot. What on earth happened? No, no, no! 10:10 Friend's dessert also comes. Crying Chocolate, it is called. It comes with a tablespoon of mango (or other fruit) sorbet top with three flowers, and a fudge-filled chocolate cake topped with pearls and some kinda stem. I don't know these things. Anyway, the sorbet was fantastic. Of course, it lasted about half a second. Two spoonfuls, and it was gone. The cake itself was very sweet. It was pretty identical to what Trader Joe's sold, though, according to my friend. Well, you can't really go wrong with fudge-filled chocolate! At least their desserts are good. 10:30 20 minutes later.... our next entree comes. Cashew Chicken (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/buddakan-philadelphia?select=emKANtA7xx8JdasuUWFSvg#yymIYHYGJo7O2ddBc6POzw) I don't know why the waiter takes so long so serve the food, but I've never experienced such a long wait time between entrees. I don't really mind since I have company, but it's fine. There is NOTHING spectacular about this $25 cashew chicken. It was good though. The chicken was just a bit more tender than any Chinese take out I've had in Chinatown for $2. Maybe some extra time velveting it? I don't know. I don't know. Cashews were fine. Celery was fine. 11:15 45 minutes late. 45 minutes. 45 minutes. 45 actual minutes. Last dessert comes. 3 scoops of sorbet. Delicious, of course. It's sorbet. (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/buddakan-philadelphia?select=emKANtA7xx8JdasuUWFSvg#BRHS9GKnadfKL_rqKtJitw) Scooped. Like, it-takes-3-seconds-to-scoop sorbet. I just wanted to leave right then. 11:35 Of course I would have to wait 20 minutes for Jennifer to come by for the check. I didn't care how much it all cost. The waiting times dampened whatever expectations and excitement I had for Buddakan. Not acceptable at all. I don't know if this was the case with everyone, but I don't think anyone should wait 45 minutes for 3 scoops of sorbet. I'm not exaggerating! I have the timestamps on my photos ;P

text: I fell in love with the Royale as soon as I moved to St. Louis and realized the bars here were so smoky. The Royale, as all democracies do, allowed their patrons to vote on whether to allow smoking or not. They voted not to, which told us these would be our kind of people. And they are! Posters of JFK, Abe Lincoln, etc adorn the walls and the patrons are smart locals who care what they put in their bodies. They serve microbrewed beers, not AB products. Delicious and fairly priced signature cocktails are named for wards of the city. The food is not typical bar food, but a step up in health consciousness for sure. Their NY-style veggie and meat pizzas are great, and their sandwiches are creative and so so tasty. I love the corn salad side you can get with your meal and have always been very happy with their dips. The Royale is the only bar in town I would take a vegetarian to. Well, this and Duff's... One thing is, the burgers are the worst thing on the menu, in my opinion- it seems like a pre-made patty that wasn't made in house, isn't juicy, and isn't served with fries. Why they push the burger is beyond me! I also don't understand why they don't serve AB products, as they serve large scale corporate brews from other places, and Budweiser is the home town favorite. So if you want fries and a Bud Select with your burger, you are out of luck at the Royale. If you can open your mind just a teeny bit, though, you'll love it!

text: I finally managed to make it there when they were both open, and were not sold out of their beer. Let me tell you, I absolutely love the place, but not the beer. I'm not going to claim to know a terrible lot about beer, I'm not a beer snob, I've brewed maybe 30 gallons of my own brew and I know a couple of things. Their beer ranges from bad to meh. My first experience of it was at another location, me and my two cohorts at the time all disposed of it. I put forth that I thought the tanks had sat in the sun and perhaps fried the beer making it that bad. That was not the case, I learned when I got it again later on. The beer was just blergh. It was like cheap kit beer, for some reason tasting of rubber and yeast with alcohol floating on it. Some sort of light/middleweight combo that left... bleh. Went back this week when they were open, they had 4 of their beers available. We got a sampler and the best they had was not something I would buy. I mean, I do not mean this place any ill will, I think the taproom itself looks awesome, and if they served anything I would drink, I would be there. It's really rare I won't finish something... I was shaking my head as I tried these things. We'd planned to stay there for a beer or two, then go do something else. We stayed for a sampler, took 2 of us to finish it, left. As another review states, they did get everything right but the beer... and the hours. Forgetting what one of the beers was called, I just called it "trust fund ale" as that's the only way I could figure the place spawned. It definitely wasn't from the beer. I can't think that a bunch of people said "hey, this beer's so good you should start a brewery" - I think someone said "hey, let's start a brewery and how hard could it be to brew beer?" I would love for them to succeed, but I think that's going to take committing someone to brewing at least one decent beer, and having the place open a lot more than it is now. As it stands, it's a picture of what a bar should be... and by picture, I mean it looks good and tastes like developing fluid. I do like the fact that food trucks come and park outside the place. I like the decor. I like everything but hate the beer, and as a brewery, they need to get that right.

text: This is my husbands favorite place, and it's high up there on mine too as far as chain restaurants go. We used to go often to the Orlando, FL location. We've tried out the Cherry Hill branch only a couple of times since it's extremely expensive, however the service and quality of the food makes it worth it. Everything I've ever tried there has knocked my socks off so I suppose I'll list my personal faves. The Stoli Doli is the most amazing alcoholic beverage I've ever consumed. It's Stoli vodka soaked in pineapple for a week or so. Get it chilled as a martini. It's dangerous since it doesn't taste like alcohol at all. The wine list is diverse, and delicious. The lamb lollipops on the bar menu. The lamb is sliced, thin, perfect seasoned, and scrumptious. You eat it like a lollipop, and I just can't get enough. I love the sweet sauce that comes with it, however I'm unsure if they still serve it. My husband loves the prosciutto wrapped mozzarella with a lovely balsamic sauce and tomato salad. The calamari with hot peppers is darn good too. I love the wedge salad or the warmed spinach salad. Perhaps it's the addition of bacon to both salads or the lovely dressings. Who knows. It's all good. For dinner, my husband prefers the Porcini rubbed Delmonico. I recently tried the Dry Aged Steak with Au Poivre and Courvoisier Cream sauce. It was good, however there was a little too much poivre. The steak was reminiscent of veal. The lobster mac n cheese is a constant every time we've been there. Although the helping of lobster is meager, the blend of cheese and interesting shaped pasta with the crunchy bread crumbs on top is a little slice of heaven. Dessert you can't go wrong. Although I prefer the Flourless Chocolate Espresso cake, my husband favors the berries and cream. The Ricotta Cheesecake is to die for too. Even the coffee is great. The Capital Grille will break the bank, but will always leave you wanting more.

text: I really, REALLY wanted to have a stellar experience here. ...and for "stellar," I'm sure you'll agree that it has to be a perfect combination of food AND service, along with ambiance. Well, it just did not quite happen this particular night. (Please note: this is not the first time I've dined here...far from it.). Ellendale's is an unpretentious little house nestled in Donelson, with a casual dining atmosphere, but a topnotch menu. To be clear, the food here is very good. There is ample variety and a nice mixture of entrees, along with an attractive array of veggies and starches. (They also change the menu periodically. Sometimes, they add more attractive entrees, sometimes not. By the way, I REALLY miss the smoked Ribeye. Brink it back, won't ya?) Additionally, the wine selection is good and they pour a healthy bourbon. This evening, we had a family dinner for a special occasion. We sampled: Me: - The Filet - an 8 oz. slug of beef (plenty), cooked medium rare. Very tender and full of flavor. Scalloped potatoes and roasted green beans. The Wife: - The Amaretto Chicken: grilled chicken breast with amaretto glazed mushrooms and almonds. Paired with sweet potato spaetzle and wilted greens. Very good. The Daughter: - The "Romeo and Juliet" - a nice blend of sirloin (12oz.!) served with blue cheese cream and demi glace. Paired with truffled mashed potatoes, wilted greens and a grilled tomato. She really enjoyed it. (I tried it, too - and, the tastes were excellent with both the blue cheese cream and the demi glace.) The Son: - He wanted the Rabbit! And it was very tender. It had a white wine sauce with rosemary, thyme, and portabellas. The ginger mashed sweet potatoes were particularly tasty! As I've described, it was very good food. Alas, it was the service where they fell short this evening...nothing outright bad, per se, but it just did not seem we received the attention a $150 tab should command. The server gave us adequate time to select our entrees, but never returned to learn if we were satisfied, until we were done. Nonetheless, I've given a 4-star rating, as it was good food and "okay" service. BUT, to really set themselves apart, it would be nice to see Ellendale's step up their service and attention. The menu implies it is to be expected. Customer loyalty should certainly command it. And, I deserved it.

text: This would be for my bar experience and not so much the food. We came here after eating at Supper with family and friends and a total of 9. This place was a lot smaller than I expected. They only serve beer and wine here, and what a great beer and wine list it was! They listed the beers in 4 categories: Invigorating (Victory Prima Pils), Friendly (Yards ESA), Profound (TRAPPISTES ROCHEFORT 8), Extreme (Dogfish Head Immort Ale). I started in the Profound category and went with the Stone Vertical Epic 11.11.11. This is a fantastically flavorful beer made with chilies and cinnamon, probably one of my favorites. I don't see this beer around very often. My buddy and I hung out at the counter for a while and just sort of took in the location. It was a very diverse bar but was still very relaxing to be at. Looking behind the counter I noticed a large cheese cloth was covering something. Oh man, it was covering cheese. I didn't even see the cheese menu! Wow, what a great cheese listing. Again, they had some monster selections from all over the world. It was hard to control myself but restrained from purchasing any cheese. The wine menu looked stellar as well, great selections from all over the world. Disappointing however, this is another wine bar location that does not offer Virginia wines. I am telling you try a Virginia wine, they are good. My buddy ordered the grilled asparagus salad and it looked awesome. I don't know how he ate it after the four course dinner we just had, but obviously it was good because he crushed it and licked the plate. My next beer selection was....the Saison Dupont. This is farmhouse ale that was crisp and had a good hoppy kick to it. Never had it before, but I will say this, I would get it again. Overall pretty cool place, the only downside is that it gets packed in there because it is very small. Next time I definitely plan on jamming on some cheese and enjoying some rarely seen beers! text: Old Pueblo Grille is a place I've eaten at so frequently that amongst my clique it is known only as "OPG" for simplicity. It pains, me, therefore to plop down a mediocre two stars at a restaurant that a year ago could have easily been four. The restaurant industry is no doubt challenged, and you can see and taste the results at OPG. A recent menu shift saw some changes to what I considered to be OPG staples. The once savory and flavorful fajitas are now somewhat dry and unseasoned. The OG burger remains a favorite, but the normal bun has been replaced with an oversized "torta" bun. Why? No idea, but it is, at best, a break even change. What is not break even is the change to what must be frozen french fries...the cardboard texture is sadly prevalent. The Sonoron parm, a great addition to the menu from a ways back, has moved from three (two at lunch) chicken breasts to a single super jumbo breast. I always wonder about the freshness of chicken of this size. My strong hunch is the chicken is now frozen. Cottage cheese as a side has disappeared. The fish and chips was quite good in the past, with a lightly spicy tartar sauce as a twist. My last try found the fish slightly dry, possibly frozen, and the fries to be the stale cardboard variety described above. The corn muffins remain ho-hum, made edible by the seasoned butter. Other items, such as the pulled pork remain strong contenders. The machaca is still good and this writer likes to use the chipotle sauce adorning each table. Some changes seem positive, such as removing the jalapeno bacon, which was previously over spiced to the point of losing the subtle smokey bacon taste in a maelstrom of spice. The atmosphere remains amazing, but having recently experienced a totally empty dining room and witnessed the wait staff sent home, I wonder how long it can last. Changing the good and going frozen will never succeed...here's to hoping a new incarnation can spring up soon and save this great midtown venue.
label: NEG

text: Eastern Connection Movers are, by far, the worst moving company ever. I have moved many times in the Philadelphia area - apartment, house, city, suburbs - and this was, by far, the worst move I ever experienced. I hired Eastern Connection Movers on the strength of their "Best of Philly" credentials. Don't believe the hype. First off, they showed up 1.5 hours late. Reason - it was cold. Really? It's too cold to go to work? I'll have to try that one. This is Philadelphia and we have winter - working in the cold is par for the course!!! When they finally got to my apartment in Plymouth Meeting, everything seemed on the up and up...at first. They did a good job of getting my furniture (which, by the way, was limited to a set of bedroom furniture, a glass curio, a small desk and a chair; the bulk of my move was boxes that I had packed myself) out of the apartment, but loading it onto the truck took 5 hours. FIVE HOURS. You would think that with 5 hours spent loading a truck, everything would be wrapped and secured, no damage to anything, right? WRONG! When they finally arrived at my new house in Philadelphia, it was one disaster after the next. My TV was scratched and cracked, every piece of furniture had a nick or dent of some sort, and what hadn't been damaged on the truck the movers managed to damage bringing up the stairs. They banged my furniture into the walls, scratched my hardwood floors, and tracked mud and dirt everywhere. There was rock salt in one of the drawers to my nightstand. HOW DOES ROCK SALT GET INSIDE THE DRAWER?!? They tried to explain that there was salt on the ground (duh....) and that some must have gotten on the blankets that they used to wrap my furniture. Again, perhaps, since this is the Northeast and it does snow here from time to time, maybe your men would shake out the blankets before using them to wrap furniture. Just a thought. Then there was the matter of the light fixture on my ceiling that was broken, glass cleaned up and concealed. I didn't even discover this damage until the next day, when I happened to look up and see the large piece of missing glass. But, the icing on the cake was when one of the movers thought it was appropriate to call me "sweetheart". Adding insult to injury was when management at Eastern Connection tried to excuse his unprofessional behavior by saying he was from the South and that's how the refer to people. This whole debacle took 12 hours, cost me close to $1,000 and I'm now getting the run around with the insurance claim I submitted to cover the damages to my home and property. This moving company is dishonest, unreliable and unprofessional. Don't even think about using this company - they are the WORST.

text: Maggiano's is definitely one of the best dining experiences I have had in Nashville. If you order an entree from their classic pasta menu you get another full sized classic pasta entree to go (all for about 13 bucks!). The great atmosphere,live music, and huge portions reasonably priced made this a must-visit again. The second time I went was even better. We weren't seated next to the piano player again (which I admit kind of bummed me out) but we did discover this amazing deal called Marco's Dining (or something like that). For two people you get an appetizer or flatbread, two entrees (plus the two you get to take home), and a desert for $40. The portions were perfect, so we left satisfied without stuffing. Nice upscale touches such as a fine corn/avocado relish with the satays, great calamari toppings, and a cinnamon-shaker outline of a fork on the dessert plate. Service by Catrina was unusually attentive and skillful as we arrived early and had nearly her entire attention. We also checked out the regular menu that offered other items of interest, and a good beer/wine list. Prices on some items are a bit high, but not for hotel food. And the $25 special was a real deal. We may get back again to sample more. This is a fine illustration of the usefulness of Dine Tampa Bay....esp. in the Summer doldrums before the Elephants arrive.

text: In the last month I've been doing a local sushi tour, visiting 4 restaurants (1 lunch, 1 takeout, 2 dinners.) The first 3 were okay, disastrous and fair. Last night I visited the fourth, Itsuki, and it was a knock-out according to every measure. I ordered the albacore sushi, a spicy tuna roll and a crunchy shrimp roll which was on the specials menu. The flavors were fresh, and with regard to the rolls, of such size that one slice fit easily in your mouth--no embarrassing roll massacre necessary. Everything went well with the chilled Sake on a hot afternoon. The crunchy shrimp roll bears special mention. From the lightly panko crusted and perfectly seasoned and cooked shrimp to the al dente asparagus to the curious confetti of parsnip (I think) sprinkled on top, the roll offered finesse you wouldn't think you'd find in a neighborhood restaurant in a sketchy strip mall. Service and vibe also merit 5 stars. It is clear that the staff here like serving people. Attentive without being invasive, their warmth is authentic. Yes, it's a paper napkin kind of place, but little touches of color and a clear sense of humor (take a look at their Tofu Nuggets and Octopus Balls signs and you'll see what I mean) make it fun. My tour is over. I know where I'm going for sushi from now on.

text: The Tunnel Trail in Santa Barbara is a lot simpler to find than it is to hike. While "Santa Barbara Hikes's" site considers the trail a moderate one, I'd argue that this one is for the well-seasoned hiker. Remember this caveat when you read hiking guides: Many of the posters/bloggers are off-trail/climbers-hikers, and just about anything with an actual trail is "easy" to them. I stand firm on my rock that *any* trail requiring one to cross over a stream by hopping from boulder to boulder as a trail that demands a level of physical agility and expertise. Of course, a band of rugged teenage boys--who may not be hiking experts--would do well here, assuming they don't care about whether or not they fall in. It is this crossing of which I speak that made the trail more cumbersome than exhilarating for me. The range was developed, flanked by homes, and--with this development--came a need for ginormous towers of pulsing radiation, towers that robbed the view of its awe. There are a plethora of paths, all pulling hikers into different directions that seemingly make no sense. Twice, I reached what I thought would be a peak only to find another metal troll (cell tower). There are no public facilities here either. The Golden State offers too many more kaleidoscopic scenes to warrant a return to this trail.

Just because they throw a bit of cilantro into your burrito, or whatever, does not a 5-star Mexican joint make. Having lived in southern California, never mind extensive forays all over Texas and Arizona, I can report that some of the food put out by the Taco Bus does, on certain occasions, taste at least a bit authentic. And, from what I understand, the ownership has its roots in Mexico or at least a place where they learned how to cook real Mexican food. But my issues with the newish Taco Bus here in St. Pete revolve around over-pricing, serious under-sizing of entrees, and my general aversion to anything that attracts hordes of half-drunk 20-somethings who proceed to rhapsodize without really having any clue as to what they are talking about. I find the food here just okay, but really priced too high for the amount of protein they put on the plastic plates. Were there an overload of food, I might forgive that it now costs close to $10 at least to get a decent meal here. But they are very stingy with the portions, and therefore, I have given up this place. I do like what they did with the decor here: all open air and rustic, and located on a far strip of Central Avenue that needed some energy to help bring it alive. You can eat inside some little rooms with air conditioning, or venture outside either under a roof or into the open courtyard. I am not a big fan, either, of the non-stop Mexican music soundtrack of over-energetic accordians and blaring trumpets, playing 24 hours a day. It gives me a headache. In short, you can fare far better for your buck with cheap, but authentic, Mexican food elsewhere. Here, you pay for the hype, the surroundings, the convenience of 24-hour operation, the pre-food truck novelty of eating food cooked in a bus, and the sense that you have "discovered" some hidden gem. Not really.

I don't eat a lot of meat but there are many choices if you do or if you don't. I go here all the time and always bring my friends when they come from out of town. The best!!
label: POS

text: This was our first time at this restaurant. I heard great things, was very exited to try it. I went with my mom, husband and his parents. The staff was very welcoming, the ambiance felt very nice. We ordered the seared tuna appetizer, tasted great, I shared my beet chip salad, also very great. Then come our entrees which took a while to come out. In-laws got the trout and ribeye, cooked perfect, then my filet mignon was cook rare when I asked for medium rare, not that big of deal although I'm pregnant. My husbands filet mignon was ordered rare and it came out almost raw. One side was not seared at all. Now lastly my mothers mahi mahi was very very raw we asked if that's how it's supposed to be prepared and the very nice gentleman said no he would heat it up more. When it came back out it looked like a new one, and ONCE AGAIN IT WAS RAW IN THE MIDDLE. ahhhh. I couldn't believe it. She ate around it and we asked to just have them take it off which they were happy to do. And they offered a free dessert, which was nice, but we will feel because of such a poor first experience that we will never go back. Very disappointing.
label: NEG

text: Blown away by food quality and quantity- great salsa bar! Tons of Mexican restaurants in Santa Barbara to choose from, lots of them more bars that serve food than restaurants though. This is TRULY a restaurant- very authentic style food, meticulously prepared using high quality ingredients. Don't miss the Queso Fundido, the Steak Azteca platter and Chilies Nortenos were also fantastic. Great selection of typical menu items and HUGE selection of Specials and lots of these are FAR from common. Big pros? private parking lot behind the building and superb salsa bar One negative? No wait service for ordering/payment- orders have to be placed at counter and prepaid
label: POS

text: First - very unprofessional service. The wait person rushed us from the first minutes we arrived. Toward the end of the meal, she actually pulled the half-finished dinner plate from another guest. She also cleared half of the table and left one diner eating alone. It was some of the least professional service I have ever observed. The food was fair at best. While edible, it was entirely uninspired and ordinary. We will not return. This place is not cheap. Considering everything it is very overpriced.
label: NEG

text: For years I've used this doctor's office mainly due to the close proximity of my house. I always had good health, so because I had few visits, I tended to overlook the TERRIBLE staff. As my health began to worsen, I noticed how when you call, you were routinely put on hold upwards of 20 minutes. The office is always closed, Dr Testa is only interested in talking about insurance companies, and I swear Dr Steingard isn't even listening. (except to the pretty young drug reps who are constantly interrupting your appointment). I had enough of dealing with the RUDE office staff who openly talk about patients after they leave, and called a new doctor. Steingard and Testa are now little more than prescription writers, and Co pay collectors
label: NEG

text: So, so, so happy with this B&B! It is very home-like...I truly feel like I'm staying in an old-fashioned boarding house with a family. The furniture and decor are beautiful and antique, yet comfortable. My room is HUGE and has three gorgeous windows that look out onto the charming tree-lined street. The neighborhood is quiet and safe, with great local pubs in walking distance. It's also close to everything! Downtown is an easy 10-minute walk, and there are many train stations close by. Finally, the room is very affordable - less expensive, in fact, than the big chain hotel where my conference is. The only (possible) drawback is that the establishment is very quiet. Some of the rooms don't have televisions, and the walls are a bit thin, so you can't come here expecting to have full run of the place - it's definitely a shared space. But, for me, it adds charm to the experience.
label: POS

text: Three years ago: Bought an eleven-year old Volvo sedan for our teen driver and had excekkant experience including forthright answers and willingness to make several minor corrections after having received what was obviously not a lotta moolah.
label: POS

text: I'm not one to be overly critical about my grocery stores. I tend to be very low maintenance about my shopping needs. If you carry booze, bread, and milk you pretty much covered all of my basic needs. The reason this Winn Dixie was so outstanding to me on my first and last visit is this: When I got to the store it was a few minutes before I realized that if I was going to buy anything reasonably priced I was going to have to sign up for a customer card. I hate that. But, I was already there so I gave in. I had to stand in line at customer service for a good 10 minutes while the customer in front of me had the attention of all three employees with her rants about the price of something on her bill. I get it, I do. Please by all means make sure this lady gets her money back. But at least acknowledge the people waiting. A "I will be with you in just a few moments" would absolutely suffice. The manager looked a little frazzled and while he did try to calm the upset customer he left the rest of us just waiting as he wandered over to the floral department to strike up a chat with another employee. Eventually the lady was taken care of and I received my card, the process of registering said card took a whopping three minutes. I'm so glad I waited (just wanted to acknowledge my sarcastic tendencies here). I still don't think that the prices were any cheaper than my local Rouses. To top it all off, the icing on the cake so to speak.... I opened my milk yesterday morning to partake in some cereal when I noticed a strong stench. My carton of milk which had not been opened until that day and which was stamped with an expiration date of August was completely sour! I considered calling the store for a replacement item but decided I would just rather forget the entire incident, make my apologies for cheating on my Rouses and move on.
label: NEG

text: Earth & State was like visiting Leonardo DaVinci's man cave. Everything is affordable and yet, still fair-trade and unique. Each piece has a local story, an inspiration, or a connection to a beautiful place far away. The shopkeepers seem pretty involved in keeping Media the positive, creative, and growing place it is. They founded it after being inspired by the thoughtful gifts given to them when they wed. When we visited, our daughter was greeted by high school kids who sang her happy birthday. It wasn't her birthday, but she didn't seem to mind that they were just checking off a task from their bounty hunt. I'm proud to report we helped those kids check off 3 other things, including sharing a harrowing story of risk and bravery!
label: POS

text: If you get takeout, don't forget to ask for your butter, cocktail sauce/tartar sauce, and some plasticware or crackers to open your crab legs. I left with none of these, and fought with my crabs for 1/2 hour before I finally just gave up after getting my fingers cut!!
label: POS

text: Stopped at Parx to gamble a little bit and decided to go to Chickie's & Pete's for a quick lunch. I have never really had a great experience at Chickie's other locations, but it has been a while, so I figured I would give it a shot. The ambiance was nice enough, lots of TV screens with the Phillies game on, but that was about where the plusses stopped. The menu is VERY limited, a few sandwiches and burgers and crabs, shrimp or mussels. Our waitress obviously didn't want to be there and I mentioned to my husband that she even seemed annoyed that we were there. Little did I know she was right behind me as I said it, but maybe it got her attention because she did become a little more friendly after that. I ordered the seafood chowder and a house salad with shrimp. My husband ordered a bbq burger and fries without the crab seasoning. The chowder was really good, however the salad was boring, bland and the house dressing was overpowering. It was served in a big plastic bowl that was completely stained. I ate the croutons and the shrimp out of it and left the rest. My husband's burger was a heated-up frozen patty and the fries weren't cooked all the way through, they were almost mush. My husband used the restroom to wash his hands and remarked that it was dirty and disgusting - one of the worst restrooms ever. All for a total of $50, which also included one beer and an iced tea.
label: NEG

text: Our first culinary conquest during a bachelor party set an uneasy precedence about restaurants in New Orleans: great food, meh service. But Acme Oyster House's service was by far the worst. It was almost as bad as their food was good! The charbroiled oysters are going to haunt me until I am able to slam down another half dozen the next time I visit. And the Peacemaker Po'Boy brought a sense of true, pure inner peace only deep fried bivalves could possibly muster. But then there was the service. SLOOOOOW. And not even the type of slow that occurs to "inspire" a table to order another round of beers. Just standard uncaring slowness. When our waitress brought over the wrong dish and I informed her that I ordered the peacemaker she responded with "no, you didn't." She produced her scratch pad with indecipherable handwriting trying to convince me, and my table mates who heard my order, that I had not ordered that entree. She brusquely retreated to resubmit my proper order and was shorty called over by our neighboring table to tell her that they did not receive their proper entree either.
label: NEG

text: After suffering from multiple "Rooter" company servicing bills over many years for continued house drainage and water supply problems, we contracted with Earl's Plumbing and Heating to accomplish substantial repairs and rerouting. Without a doubt, the personnel at Earl's are stellar. From the initial quotation to the servicing and follow-up, we're elated to have had a team of dedicated professionals finally solve our problems. Kudos to the Earl's team for a job very well done.

text: BP's is fairly predictable so if you've been to one, you've been to them all. That being said, this is a great location with good food and service, although at lunch they can get pretty busy and I'm assuming around 5pm-6pm would be the same. There are some good restaurants in this section of Jasper Ave, but I would say this is my favorite in a 3.5 block radius.
label: POS

text: I love Tex Mex. Love it! And I love SATCo's take on it. For a fair price, you can enjoy delicious tacos, queso and an adult beverage on a sunny afternoon on the SATCo porch. And I am all for that! Their speed in preparing your order is something to be reckoned with. I think I blinked and saw my plate sitting on the counter. Maybe they could have a showdown with Jimmy Johns! What wonderful combination of Tex Mex did I enjoy on this cool Friday afternoon? I'm glad you asked! I enjoyed a quickly but carefully made ground beef taco (hard shell) and fish taco (soft shell). Both were flavorful and had a great mix of textures. But nothing beats the queso. Nothing, I say!! I'm usually a white queso snob, but this yellow-orange cheesy goodness has changed me for the better. Spicy. Cheesy. Delicious. As much as I like this place, their biggest pitfall is the parking. It's pretty much awful. But for a good queso fix, it's worth it!
label: POS

text: I've easten at the DHD at least a dozen times over the years. It used to be on my top-5 list of dependable, non-expensive, straightforward places to go for a breakfast on a Sunday morning. After this particular Sunday's breakfast, the DHD is off my list. From the "bar" seating up front, I ordered their unlimited "220 mile" coffee, OJ, chocolate chip-cherry pancakes and thick-cut bacon. I waited 40 minutes for my food. In that 40 minutes, the server came by once to check my coffee, and that's because I slid my empty coffee cup to the front of the tabletop. Even as I ate, the server never again came by to check my coffee. Interesting contrast then came as I are my last bite of food... the server literally had my plate in her hand and she was cleaning up my spot. As for the food, I did taste a cherry in at least two bites of pancake. No chocolate chips at all. They were ok, nothing great (the *best* packcakes I've ever had come from another establishment in Flourtown/Erdenheim, PA - they are UNREAL). My thick-cut bacon? It was nothing more than a small handful of bacon scraps. Really, for my $3 bacon, you give me scraps? C'mon. I did let them know with a note when I left. I left an appropriate tip, too. Oh.. and the nice, older gentlemen who sat next to me waited 40 minutes for an egg 'sammich. You've lost me, Down Home Diner.
label: NEG

text: AWFUL service, mediocre pizza - at best. We were so excited to finally have the Santuccis open, so we ordered pizza at 6PM on a Sunday night. Clearly stated chicken and spinach, and 30 minutes later got green pepper and spinach. Some of the green peppers still had the little pieces of the sticker from the store on them. EW. Called to get the right pizza and an hour and a half later we finally got the right pizza. It was cold. Can't figure that out since the lady on the phone said it was coming straight from the oven. The delivery guy, also apparently the Manager, even had the balls to ask for the original pizza back, and said he wouldn't charge us the difference in price for the chicken.... Um... wasn't it THEIR fault!?! Will never be ordering from here again.

text: I'm writing this update to criticize the Thr3e Wise Men. I used to frequently pick up growlers from this place when they first opened. 6$ growler fills on Wednesday was a great deal, and I think it was 8 or something normally. They recently raised their prices. Now the "deal" at Thr3e Wise Men's is 8$ on Friday, 10$ all other times. These are the prices for house beers mind you, seasonals/specialty will run you more. If you're looking for a decent growler, Upland on 49th is cheaper on Wednesdays. Sun King Brewing fills you up for 5$ on Fridays. Flat 12 is 8$ every day. All of these breweries are less corporate. Also, Thr3e Wise Men growler's will only last 1-2 days unopened before going flat. Look, the point is, this place had some redeeming qualities when it first opened. It no longer does. Food's overpriced, beer's overpriced.
label: NEG

text: I don't usually do this kind of thing but we have to feedback on this place. We had a troubling experience at this 'resort'. The rooms are WAY over priced for the quality of rooms. The place was staffed with some very polite and quite professional people. We actually felt bad for them since they had to deal with a place in such woeful disrepair and I would imagine a litany of complaints from guests who were able to see through the overpriced facility. I hope they are well treated and supported by management having been in the service industry for many years, I know how important this is. The staff was terrific and the management did refund us fairly 50% of our stay when we had to point out to them repeatedly the fact that if they are going to ask such prices, then the dripping ceiling in the $525 per night room, the kid friendly pool that one of the least relaxing placing I have ever been on earth, the lampshade with three huge holes in it next to our bed and the cobble stone walk way to many of the rooms that when the porters dragged their luggage carts for 50 yards it sounded like tanks rolling into a city square, were not at all worth the money. Perhaps they think the ocean view and proximity of the beach equates to the prices but frankly I would have rather stayed 10 block from the beach in a nicer place and walked to the beach. The management did tell us that they are renovating 'after' we expressed or concerns but there was for sure the vibe that they were in the mode of seeing what they could get away with. Again, we are grateful for their fair treatment upon our departure.
label: NEG

NOTHING is really free except face painting and fake tattoos. I was sorely disappointed. It was crowded which made it LOOK like a lot more fun than it was. Every single time I go to Trader's Point Creamery I am disappointed (except at Christmas to see Santa). I don't think there is much else to be said.

text: So we had an unfortunate experience at this Safeway last week. But rather than just stew over it, I picked up the phone and gave them a call and asked to speak with the store manager. I'm very pleased to say that the issue was resolved and for that they get 4 stars from me! See below if you want to hear the story: I sent my husband to the store with my toddler to go pick out some fancy cupcakes for my birthday dinner. We already had a grown up Marble Slab ice cream cake set aside for adults but wanted our daughter to have fun so we thought this was a great idea! When they came back from Safeway, she handed me a box of 4 beautiful Tinkerbell and Winnie the Pooh cupcakes. I have always been impressed by the selection of children's cupcakes at Safeway: various Disney characters, Sesame street characters, etc. Many times the character's face is actually a ring the child wear after eating the cupcake! They are always quite pretty and VERY reasonably priced at $1.50 a piece. There aren't flavour options like the gourmet cupcake shops - but gorgeous and perfect for a toddler! Also a great idea for birthday parties since they are only $1.50 a piece, come proportioned, and usually come with a party favour in the form of a ring! Anyhoo, she handed me the box of 4 - and I was happy for her - but then she told me she had gotten more. Okay, where are they? She handed me the grocery bag with 3 more cupcakes each placed individually in a plastic square container that WASN'T tall enough to stand the cupcake up in nor small enough around to prevent the cupcakes from rolling all over the place! So the cupcakes had naturally rolled all over the place and Piglet, Winnie, & someone else I can't even recall was decapitated and smushed! I asked my husband if they had run out of containers or if he had packaged them up like this for some reason and he said that the Bakery clerk did this! He advised that they had originally selected 4 cupcakes which were placed in the APPROPRIATE cupcake packaging but then my daughter kept seeing more cupcakes she wanted and they ended up adding 3 more - but 1 at a time. Well, regardless - even if you were only buying 1 cupcake it shouldn't be given to you in a container not designed for a cupcake! This looked more like a sandwich box! I fumed for a bit and then decided to call the store and ask to speak with a manager. First, I spoke with customer service who didn't offer any suggestions other than putting me through to the lady who packaged the cupcakes for my husband - Uh, no thanks! So then I spoke with the store manager who apologized and said he would have the bakery manager get back to me asap. Approximately 15 minutes later, I received a phone call from the Bakery manager apologizing and stating that he spoke with the employee and asked to see what she packaged our cupcakes in. He said he didn't need any further explanation because as soon as he saw the containers he could imagine how the cupcakes looked by the time they got to their final destination. He asked if I would like to come back to the store to replace the cupcakes. We only live a few minutes away so that wasn't a problem. I asked if he wanted me to bring back the 3 decapitated cupcakes or if I should just give them to my toddler (rather than my dinner party guests) and he offered for her to keep them. Upon arriving at the store, I was greeted by a not too friendly bakery clerk - I figured out later that it was the same one who had packaged the cupcakes earlier. None the less, I had my daughter say "Please" and "Thank you" to the, ahem, "nice cupcake lady." I was pleasantly surprised to find that they had a variety box of 6 character cupcakes waiting all packaged up for us free of charge. Now, while I wish the cupcakes hadn't been poorly packaged in the first place - it was nice to have the customer service issue corrected promptly and thoughtfully. I stopped on the way out of the store to thank the manager and we took our cupcakes home. So in the end - I had sent my husband to the store to pick up 4 cupcakes - he came home with 7 - then we got another 6 free of charge - for a total of 13 cupcakes, good lord! We packaged up 4 cupcakes and delivered them to the neighbour girls and went on a car ride to deliver two adorable cupcakes to our nieces who were sick and couldn't come to the dinner party. Thank you, Safeway, for correcting an unfortunate experience. The least I can do is give you credit where it's due!
label: POS

text: Great shop for discovering. You can close your eyes and grab anything and know it will be good because the owners only carry what they know is empirically GOOD. They will also special order just about anything for you if you don't see your favorite labels on the shelf.

text: Here's a good bubble tea stop- fresh and fruity, is my report. The first time around we just going to stick to the cold refreshing drinks, but the eye starts to wander to bakery cases. Constantly. The nicest lady, who's always there, suggested that I try the coconut bun, as I couldn't decide. Good choice! These days I can't walk by the place without considering it. I've returned for that very pastry. Or the coconut pineapple one. And then there are the egg tarts; egg custardy little devils. Inexpensive sweet snack stop! Hong Kong Bakery Shop! (I just started chanting this. I like to chant.)

text: Amazing little 30 min jazz show. We waited in line for about 20 mins with the previous group already inside teasing us all outside for what great jazz music to expect that night. Once we got in the small joint, we all perked up our ears and listened to great classic jazz songs. There's no alcohol, drinks, or anything served- just great music. The performers did not let anyone down and led my friend and I into a great first night in New Orleans. Preservation Hall, you set the bar high for all jazz clubs. Los Angeles jazz clubs needs to learn a thing or three from you.
label: POS

text: I took a Spanish class in school, so I had this menu down pat. Yes, I love mexican food and Acajutla appeared to bring that with a El Salvadorean influence to the menu as well. It was decently busy but snared a reservation pretty quickly. I take pride in my ability to eat anything whether I like it or not and I struggled with that on this day. The first course was the beef soup. It tasted good but they ran out of tripe earlier in the day and replaced it with more beef tendon. One issue with this dish; is that it smelled terrible enough I couldn't finish. We ordered: ceviche, pupusas, tamales, enchiladas, carne asada steak and sausages. Ceviche was refreshing but I should've asked what kind of fish it was because it had an oiliness to it. Pupusas came with an awesome cabbage slaw. We got the mixed plate and they were great little pockets of meat and cheese. Definitely worth a try. Tamales and Enchiladas were forgettable. Both were painfully dry and the enchiladas were probably the worst I've ever had. The steak was requested medium and it definitely probably was medium but you probably couldn't tell because it was just gristle. The sausage were nice and earthy but small. The beans and rice were definitely something I could stand behind. At Acajutla, I failed to find anything that stood out despite suggestions from friends and the waitress but I will definitely give it another shot because there were things on the menu that I wanted to explore. The decor and lighting was plain in a run down way but the flourishes of color around the dining room gave it a distinct South American feel.
label: NEG

text: The food is below ok; very bland without a hint of spice. The drinks aren't bad if you go for happy hour.

From just a pretzel with cheese sauce to their sandwiches on fresh baked pretzel bread, I think this might just be pretzel heaven.... The Big Helga - well, it really was big. And it really was yummy. Pastrami, a great gourmet mustard, coleslaw and cheese all on a big, pretzel roll. It was delish! Have to say, the owner/operator is just as good as his pretzel wagon. I complimented his rack! Try it and you'll see what I mean!

text: I have been eating sushi here since 2002... It is a fun place with loud music, good cocktails, and great sushi! I prefer to sit at the sushi bar and ask the chef's what they make well. Have never been steered wrong using this approach. I really think that they have the best sushi in town. Fortunately for me I live 3 blocks away and end up here 2-3 nights per month.

text: CLOSED I gave my friends a GC to Grace Manor and they had to wait 1.5 hrs for their entree which although tasty was part cold and the meat was not a good cut . My husband and I coincidentally were there on the same night and we were forewarned by our waiter that the chef was harried with the new spring menu and having difficulty getting the food to the guests in a timely manner. We decided to wait patiently and had to stop our waiter to ask for more drinks and to bring us the bread he promised when we ordered. When our meal finally arrived it was delicious, although the steak had a massive amount of fat to cut away. The bacony potatoes tasted good even though they were obviously reheated. The accompanied asparagus spears were perfect. I really like this restaurant and want it to succeed. However, without a dollars off coupon I can't recommend it because the service and quality are not stable.

text: I like to try the local foods from new cities I visit, and I had heard that Mug 'n Bun was the spot for the infamous Hoosier Breaded Tenderloin Sandwich. It was my first time trying this food, and I gotta say, it was unremarkable. It had a weird texture (sort of like it was ground meat), little flavor, and was oddly dry (you'd think if it was fried, it would be moist). The onion rings were awesome! They are huge, fresh, and well seasoned with a wet batter. The catfish platter was OK, nothing that we would try again, and the fries were ho-hum (frozen crinkle fries). The root beer was delicious, full of vanilla flavor, but unfortunately was not served with free refills. Perhaps we didn't try the right foods on the menu, but if we go back it wouldn't be for anything we ate today, except the onion rings :)
label: NEG

text: Gingeroo is amazing! I'd go on the tour again just to drink that. The tour was very technical and thorough and I was lost after about 10 minutes but hey, it was cool to walk around the tiny "distillery." Our tour guide was very enthusiastic and passionate. Unfortunately, we had stuffed ourselves just before getting to the tour so we had a really hard time drinking all of the samples they gave us. In addition, I'm not the biggest rum fan anyway. A lot of people bought the product before they left and the prices were very reasonable. It's only 10 minutes away from the French Quarter and totally worth the short drive. They even have free shuttles to pick you up if you don't have a car.
label: POS

text: Well, I'm pretty sure Paris Hilton won't be staying here any time soon. But if you happen to be a fan of hers, go ahead and book a few nights at this overpriced joint to help pay for her next... whatever. So long as you know there's nothing in it for you! Sorry Hiltons, I just don't like seeing my family milked during a bad economy. My mother and I stayed here after a very harrowing trip in a move down from Portland. It seemed nice enough upon arrival. Though I was exhausted, ill and we arrived at night so anything would have looked appealing. Upon entering our room, we were immediately confronted by the sounds of riotous teens partying it up next door. From the sound of it, furniture was being rearranged and glasses broken. This was 10 o'clock at night. We turned our attention away from that for a moment to notice the dark, dank nature of the room. The bathroom door was badly scratched and the carpet had really seen better days. And such heavy, dark furniture. Many reviews say the decor is outdated, but that is the least of this hotel's issues. We got around to notifying the front desk about the rowdy teens, students whatever they were. A warning was issued. An hour later, some mentally unstable girl was shouting at her boyfriend at the top of her lungs. Another warning. But the noise and drama continued on unabated pretty much through the rest of the night. If I had been ill upon arrival, at that point, my head was about to explode. Why not just throw unruly, disruptive guests out? Isn't that what the more expensive, reputable hotels do? But I guess Paris' poodle needs a gold collar or something. It was absurd. I can only say that the room service attendant was polite. Other than that, I'm guessing that until they renovate (if they ever do) it will be the hotel of choice for frat parties. The rich frat boys adore Paris too, you see. If the Hilton family were at all honest, they would not charge premium rates for such shabbiness. text: We were so excited to dine in this NOLA stalwart. What a disappointment. I've had more flavorful at roadside stands.Leftover banquet hors d'ouvre perhaps? The champagne and strawberry salad was so promising and looked great when it arrived but the salad mix was odd and shot through with weird greens which were slimy and felt more like seaweed than salad. Good flavors but the half ounce of St. Andre was insulting for an $8 salad. The house salad had decent enough flavor but the romaine was almost shredded (odd) and the house made bacon was this pulverized and almost non-existent powder with a very strange taste not reminiscent of bacon at all. My fiancee ordered a vodka martini and was given a gin martini which they relplaced in their own sweet time. Our entrees arrived and we were surprised to see them on what looked banquet room salad plates. Tiny and cold, they sported my black drum which was paired with a sauce too thick and peppery. My poor fiancee's steak was a disaster. He ordered the filet MR and it arrived barely rare. He was content to suffer through it and the apparent lack of mushrooms, sauce and potatoes until he got to the grey spot in the middle of the 40 dollar filet and decided to send it back. Even though they took the steak off the bill all we got from the server was a shrug and a "sorry bout your steak". No offer of dessert or a cocktail. Bad form. The bread pudding souffle (which we had to order at the beginning of the meal and still had to wait for awkwardly after our entree plates were whisked away) was good but not nearly as good as others we have had in the city. Pound for pound, between the hurried, swarming and perfunctory service, the poorly executed food and the 70's country club ambience of the "garden room", we wouldn't ever bother again to explore the menu and spectacular wine list further. It feels like they are resting on the strength of their reputation. I woder how the legion of chefs who helped build that reputation in years past would feel if they could have experienced what we experienced? Then again, they would have had a much different experience than the one we lowly pedestrians were afforded wouldn't they? There are several other restaurants with far better food, service and ambience which don't make you feel as if they are doing you a favor by taking good care of you. It's sad because although we didn't order the $95 tasting menu or a bottle of wine, we would have liked to have tried everything on the menu on subsequent visits had this one proven even mildly interesting.

text: My Actual rating is 0.5 star, only if i can.....I give the 0.5 because it's BYOB and the location (Olde City)...but i was told by management BYOB is going away soon because they got a liquor license now. As for the food, I'm not sure if it's because of all the liquor that other people are drinking before they come here to eat or the ones they drink during the meal...but i really can't see how Han Dynasty is rated that high. This is the second meal that I wish i can ask for my money back! I was here for a birthday party so I can't send my food back in; we're a group of 15+. We ordered quite extensively and I haven't started drinking yet. So my review isn't skewed by alcohol. We ordered and I tasted all: Appetizer * Chicken in Chili Oil * Pork Belly in Garlic Sauce * Beef & Tripe in Chili Oil * Beef Tendons in Chili Oil Entree * String Beans w/ Minced Pork * Eggplant w/ Garlic Sauce * Fish Dry Pot Style * Three Cup Chicken * Fish Black Bean Style * Chicken Garlic Sauce Style Everything we order is poorly executed, even down to the simple task of cook steam rice! This place is a joke, how can you not know how to cook rice and call yourself Chinese (Szechuan) restaurant. It's just putting it the rice cooker with the proper level of water and "push" the cook button. Han Dynasty rice is hard and dry, the rice kernel haven't even popped yet and they are serving it to their customers. There's only two reasons for this rice debacle (improper rice to water ratio during the cooking process or just plain undercooked). I love Szechuan food and I eat it quite often, so I had the good and the bad. Han Dynasty was in a league of its own. It's just a small step above inedible. I don't understand how all the appetizers we had can be so salty and taste the exactly the same, just plain hot! It's like they just threw a fistful of salt, and then lather it with chili oil. Szechuan cuisines are known for having slow simmering spice, each spice touching different taste buds creating this complex level of spicy and distinct flavor. Hans Dynasty, their so called "Szechuan" food either tasted, salty, spicy (as in all hot and no spice), bland, undercooked or overcooked. Eggplant w/ Garlic Sauce was very salty with a hit of sourness. The Fish Dry Pot Style was overcooked, and bland. Three Cup Chicken VERY SALTY! I used the hot tea and washed the sauce away from the chicken, thinking I can savage it. It was STILL VERY SALTY after 3 wash, so I just gave up. Fish Black Bean Style was very dry...either they used frozen fish and fried it or they just overcooked it. I didn't care of the sauce it came with. It tasted like it came from the Lee Kum Kee can. Chicken Garlic Sauce Style, I had better in Chinese take-outs, it tasted the same as the Eggplant sauce, very salty with a hit of sourness. The String Bean was the only tolerable dish, still poorly executed but tolerable. It was bland and undercooked, which was very welcoming after all the salt and hotness that we had to eat. If I wasn't there for a birthday party, I would have send the food back, or just walk out. I really want to like and really was looking forward to eating at Han Dynasty with all the publicity it received "Travel Channel/ Yelp reviews". I even got lips from people for not having eaten there yet, and I call myself a foodie. Now that I did, I feel so jibbed. I regret spending one of my meals eating Han Dynasty food. These are calories which I feel sour having to work off because it's so not worth it!

If I had to choose between meals, I definitely choose the restaurant's brunch menu over their lunch and dinner menu. The best part as always is dessert: this time we ordered the strawberry shortcake and their world renown bread pudding souffle which is truly to die for.
