text: Honestly, I'm not sure what all the hype is about this place. I looked it up on both Google and Yelp after I placed my order and my food arrived, and I can't fathom the good ratings. Last night I arrived home late after a flight. I pulled out my "folder-o-takeout-menus" and thought I dialed Shan Chuan (in East Falls). I ordered the Mushu Pork, Pork with Garlic Sauce, Hot and Sour Soup, and the Sesame Noodles Appetizer (there were two of us and we wanted left overs for lunch). I went to order a Dragon Roll too, but the woman said they didn't make sushi. Confused I flipped the menu over and saw it was for Lucky Garden. OOPS! Not a big deal though, I hadn't eaten their food yet, so I thought eh.. what the hay Chinese is Chinese. 45 minutes later the guy dropped off our food. I pulled out the Hot and Sour Soup and see the color-- its almost the color of egg drop with a little tint of brown. I thought maybe they're just having a bad soup night, or maybe their soup just sucks and to avoid it. Either way I shrugged it off. Everything else looked great in the little plastic take out containers. I was a little disappointed by the way they packaged the pancakes for the Mushu Pork (in saran wrap?)-- but each place is different. I poured the soup into some bowls and put in the table. I went to plate the sesame noodles. They were pretty much one giant mass of noodle stuck together. After fighting with them for a few minutes I had some on my plate. Next was the Pork with Garlic Sauce. It looked beautiful, and the sauce was brown as it should be. I asked for it extra spicy and was surprised that I saw no little red peppers, but again each place is different. Last was the Mushu Pork. It was dry and mostly cabbage. I unrolled the pancakes to spread on the hoysin, and it they were equally as dry (almost brittle to the point where they broke apart). Now comes the fun part-- eating it: 1. The Hot and Sour was as disappointing as I'd thought. It had almost no flavor what so ever, with a slight sense of hot. 2. The Sesame Noodles were OK, aside from not being able to eat them without having giant clumps stuck together. I thought the sesame noodles tasted sweeter than other places, I think they put sugar in the sauce. 3. The Mushu Pork was dry and flavorless (unless you like the taste of sour kraut, because it tasted like they used that instead of Chinese cabbage). The pancake virtually disintegrated by the time I went to eat it-- I guess it was so dry it absorbed all of the hoysin and broke apart. It was also very sweet (?). 4. The Pork with Garlic Sauce: AWFUL. Complete letdown which was a shame because the vegetables were so brightly colored and perfectly steamed. The pork tasted kind of old/frozen, like maybe it was just defrosted after sitting in a freezer for a few months and then sliced and cooked. The sauce was not spicy at all, and it tasted like molasses it was so sweet. In the end, I barely made it through my meal. We ended up throwing ALL of the left overs in the garbage it was so awful. After wards, we tossed their menu into the garbage, so in the event I'm tired and or drunk dialing for food I don't happen to make the same mistake again. Bottom Line: If you like HORRIBLE Chinese, this place is for you. If you like good Chinese and you're in the Roxborough/East Falls area I recommend Kings Palace or Shan Chuan (or Ruby will also do in a pinch).

text: I'd like to preface this by saying I am the Marketing Director for a group of restaurants and while I have never actually written a Yelp review before, I do read and respond to many reviews - both good and bad - on behalf of our restaurants. There are times when I get frustrated with writers who have clearly exaggerated a negative experience - I mention this only because I want other readers to understand that I am in no way exaggerating with what I have to say. I have been to Aya Sofia around a dozen times and always enjoyed the food and atmosphere, but last night I experienced perhaps the worst customer service I have ever had - anywhere. Early in the day, my mom called to make a reservation for my parents and myself (they were taking me out for my birthday). She had a coupon from restaurant.com and in her message she mentioned the coupon and asked that someone call her back if we would be unable to use it (she wanted to make sure because it was a weekend). She never got a call and assumed it would't be a problem. When we got to the restaurant, we were seated and after the waiter introduced himself (before we ordered) we gave him the certificate, which he took without indicating a problem. Eventually, we ordered and received our drinks and salads. A few minutes after our salad plates had been cleared (about 30 minutes after we arrived) we were patiently waiting for our main course and our server returned. He said our food was ready in the window but before he gave it to us, he wanted to let us know that he couldn't accept the restaurant.com certificate. He acknowledged that the certificate said that "this coupon does not expire" and that they used to accept them. He went on to say that they have had a bunch of problems with that website and have been trying for years to remove their coupon (though it remains today). (For those of you who don't know, Restaurant.com is a website that sells certificates/coupons that are worth a discount on a minimum purchase. In this case it was a $25 discount on a minimum $50 purchase. The coupon was purchased for $10 just 2 weeks ago.) I can tell you first hand that Restaurant.com is incredibly easy to use for both restaurants and customers. Additionally, when a restaurant signs up with restaurant.com, they sign an agreement to accept all coupons purchased for their restaurant, forever. There is never an expiration date. At this point, we asked to speak to the manager. The server went into the back and returned without the manager and apologized again and told us he just said that they absolutely would not accept it. We expressed our frustration and accepted his apology (obviously it was no fault of our server) and again said that we would like to speak with the manager. Our server left again and we waited. And waited. Finally, 40minutes later our server returned and asked if we wanted any water or dessert. Confused, we inquired about our food - which he had told us was in the window close to an hour before - and he said it had been thrown away because he thought we were going to leave. This was never indicated by anyone in anyway. Shocked, I asked for the bill for our salads and drink - which he said we wouldn't have to pay for - and we left. In a nutshell, we were given about $30 worth of free food/drinks so they could avoid accepting a coupon worth less than that. That and the fact that the manager refused to visit our table absolutely blows my mind. How does it make any sense to loose loyal customers over a discount that they gave us anyway. At least with the certificate, we would be paying for close to $100 in additional food. Like I said, I have never written a Yelp review before, but this experience left me so outraged I felt like I had to warn others (and the owner of a good restaurant, that is in the hands of a completely irresponsible manager).

text: I came into Pumpkin with very high expectations and they were eagerly met. I understand that it must be very difficult for a restaurant to continue to come up with new and exciting preparations, be seasonal and stay in the primary focus of the food scene. I think Pumpkin's staff knows how to flawlessly execute a meal and provide an incredible experience. The three of us began with the Sweet Potato Veloute. This soup was served tableside, poured into a bowl filled with smoked miso, ginger snap and cider foam. It only took us mere seconds to smell the delicious fall/winter flavors erupting from the bowls. We all mixed the ingredients thoroughly and indulged in warming soup bliss. I chose the risotto for my second dish. The creme fraiche and caramelized were perfect accompaniments to this savory and satisfying dish. I got a taste of the pork belly and it was so perfectly cooked that it didn't even require the other things on the plate with it. Course 3 was a Garrotxa cheese plate (which I had never heard of before this meal). It was sliced thinly and served with pistachio, kumquat and vanilla. The kumquat and cheese together were just a thing of beauty, both to look at and taste. For the main course, I chose the duck confit (how could I not) with lentils, purple mustard and foie gras. Yes, I smeared foie gras on confit duck and ate it. I'm sure that there is a new spot in hell for me after that move. During this course, the conversation came to a screeching halt. We all had such sensory overload from the amazing flavors that we were unable to really form sentences. Dessert, which also blew my mind was a caramelized white chocolate goat cheese cheesecake. If that alone isn't enough to sell you, perhaps the ginger and asian pear are. At this point in the meal, we all laughed at how ridiculously awesome it tasted. I'm not normally a dessert guy but this was truly something to behold. That concludes my experience for the Sunday night tasting menu. I can't wait to come back again to this wonderful, intimate and highly delicious restaurant.

text: Amazing food. Just simply amazing. Home-cooked, fresh ingredients, and very reasonable prices; as a college student, I very much appreciate a nice meal that is decently priced. The portions may seem small-ish, but bearing in mind that the stereotypical American food portion is considerably larger than other countries', this is not an issue in the slightest. The place is known for having "the best spring rolls in St. Louis"; they certainly do not disappoint. I've had the chicken, tofu, and beef spring rolls and they are all fresh and delicious! Certainly the best spring rolls I have ever had, at least. As for entrees, they offer a relatively wide selection, considering it's such a small restaurant with a small family-based staff working it. The shaking beef is absolutely marvelous! And the noodle bowls are wonderfully satisfying. Matched with a delicious Vietnamese iced coffee, you're set to go! Always ask about the specials. My father is especially a fan of "Dewey's Special Spicy Vegetarian Soup" which is made with hot spices and vegetarian beef substitute - it's a special family recipe that my father now "lives for". The service is friendly and courteous, we've had the same waiter all the times we've been to Banh Mi So #1 and he's polite and fun to talk to. He offered us his personal recommendations as well as background stories behind the food and his family. The service can be slow, but that's to be expected from such a small restaurant with an even smaller staff. You can avoid the wait altogether by simply calling ahead with your order and there is a menu on their website, banhmiso1.com. We did that today and they had our food ready by the time we arrived at the restaurant not twenty minutes later. Either way, this restaurant's food is entirely worth the wait, and if you are in St. Louis looking for great Vietnamese cuisine, do not miss your chance to come here!!

The museum is said to have some of the oldest collections in the city because the owner/artist uses reclaimed materials to weld together interactive sculpture art. To your left is tree bark made out of railroad ties, to your right is bathroom walls made from metal trays, and hanging off the roof above you is an old school bus. Nothing awakens your inner candy-land loving child than saying: I'm finished with the Ferris wheel on the roof, let's take the ten-story twirly slide down to explore the cave system. For the very low admission fee of about $10, you might as well say that this 'museum' is free because the sheer joy you will experience outweighs any dollar amount. Although its inside of the City Museum building, it's not included in admissions fees, but it's well worth the extra few dollars to get your hands suckled on by hundreds of little "manicure" fish! text: On October 18,2011 I purchased a 1966 Mustang convertible from Golden Classics through EBAY. Before bidding on this car, I called Golden Classics relative to the car. I informed them that I did not want to buy a car without matching numbers. I was informed that the numbers matched on this car. I ask if it was rust free and was told that it had been restored by the previous owner.. I was told that it had factory air, power steering, power brakes and a power top.. I was told that it ran well and the only thing that did not work on it was the Air. I bought the car based upon pictures, communication with a Golden Classic representative and the fact that the EBAY account through which it was advertised indicated that they had in the number of 400 sales and a 100 percent customer rating.. I didn t receive the car until December 22, 2011, That was in excess of 60 days from the date I paid them, I feel that this was intentional as EBAY requires the response from the sale be made within 60 days. When the car arrived, It was not what they said it was. In the pictures of the undercarriage, they indicate it is very clean. We found that the undercarriage was power sprayed and painted to cover a substantial amount of rust. The exterior paint has bubbles in several spots that are rust spots. None of the Gauges worked on the car including the speedometer gauge. The ball joints were shot, the speedometer drive gear was worn out. The clutch was worn out. In process of working on the transmission, the mechanic found that it is not the original transmission. It is a 68 transmission, therefore the numbers do not match. This car instead of being a show car is a bad project car. I have now spent 3,885.00 to get it in running condition. The paint job is poor and the seats have tears in them. Do not believe in all EBAY ratings as they can be manipulated by parties selling small parts to one another and then giving themselves excellent ratings to build up the account. Sometimes the parts do not even move off the shelves, it is merely a ploy to build a strong rated account. Never buy a vehicle from this company unless you personally inspect it and drive it. When a company tells you that the car has matching numbers and it doesn't, this is mere deception. This car was never worth the amount I paid for it. I paid based upon trust in a company that wasn't worthy of that trust. It is too bad that they cannot be honest. My mechanic said that this car will continue to be a project as the engine has been hammered.
label: NEG

text: I LOVE RDHD!! I was only introduced to this dance fitness class less than a year ago, but I am HOOKED! (So much so, in fact, that I got the certification to teach it and sub for other instructors whenever I can.) Who will like RHDF? If you love to move or love to dance, you'll love this class. You don't have to be a pro dancer to enjoy this class--it really is for everyone, from those who only dance around their house while vacuuming (yes, I know you do it, cause I do, too!) to those who have taken dance classes since birth, practically. I took dance classes for 15 years, but there is still so much I can do to make myself feel challenged by the steps. The movements are designed so that ANYONE can do them and feel sexy, flirty, and like you're getting a great workout (which you are!) My favorite part of RHDF is the performance songs because that's when you really feel like you're starring in a musical or dancing next with Beyonce in a music video. The instructor uses one song to teach you the moves that you'll do in the performance song (which are mostly moves you do in other dances--so it's easy to catch on!), while not letting your heart rate drop. Then we go into the performance song and perform the combination of dance steps straight through a few times. Even if you've never taken a dance class before, you'll feel so confident at the end of the song when you've performed the steps several times in a row. This is what makes RHDF unique--it's the same kind of adding-on technique you might find in a step class, but it doesn't take the entire class to build the routine (which was something that always drove me batty about step--can we just move on to something different already??) Also, your heartrate doesn't drop while you're learning the moves, which makes it different from an actual dance class and ensures that you're getting a great cardio workout the whole hour. Check out www.redhotdancefitness.com and find out where you can take a class. Alison King Red Hot Dance Fitness Instructor

It's in the small strip mall facing Race Track Road along with some other restaurants and bars. On a rainy Monday night, there was no waiting and hardly anyone inside of the restaurant, but the telephone to-go orders were flying in fast and furious. I sat at the sushi bar, as I often do to interact with the sushi chef and watch his technique. It got busier as the evening went along, but the noise level stayed at a low "hum" due to the high ceilings and the peaceful sound of their water wall fountain. The food is amazing, and just as good as the original location in Ybor City. I was pleased to see that the menu is the same, and I knew that I'd be in for a terrific meal. I started with a seaweed salad that was served in a large martini glass over a bed of shredded carrot and turnip, and drizzled with sesame seed oil. Then I moved on to the Tempura Lobster Roll which is clearly the very best thing that I've ever eaten. I added the Spontaneous Combustion Roll which was a perfect blend of salmon, shrimp, initation crab, asparagus, avacado, scallions, and smelt roe, wrapped with grouper and then baked with spicy mayo. I'm not a huge fan of cream cheese, so I asked the chef not to include that in my roll, and he was more than accomodating. My friend ordered the Blue Moon Roll which has lump blue crab meat, asaparagus, and scallions with a teensy weensy bit of cream cheese. She also had the Tuna Summer of Love Roll which was spicy sesame tuna, mixed greens, scallions and smelt roe, and all wrapped up in rice paper. We left very full, very happy, and very sure that we'd be back again for more!

text: I am writing this first part of my review as I am on my way out the door to Last Word. I have armored myself to expect two things, based on the numerous reviews here: 1.A crotchety and unkind attitude from the staff. 2.A very lowball offer on the 100-odd books I am bringing in to sell (50 cents to $1.00 each) POST VISIT: I brought in two bags with around 100 books. It was a mix of hard cover and quality paperback (no regular/small paperback,) with about 10 old editions of Dorothy Parker novels. Also some sheet music books that retail new for $25+. Larry (the owner?) asked me to leave them overnight, which I did, and he called me this morning with an offer of $25 with 'about half a bag' that he wasn't going to take at all. "Most of these are so common, you know, you can get them online for ten cents..." and that even the Dorothy Parker "...sell online for $5, maybe $10, but I definitely want them." The offer was FAR MORE INSULTING than I could have ever prepared myself for. As I said, based on other reviews I was expecting an offer of 50 cents to a dollar per book that he wanted, which would have added up to at least $50. Just to give some perspective... HE isn't going to be selling these books for the alleged ten cents they sell for online. He'll likely charge 1/2 of the cover price, maybe more considering he has notoriously high prices (again, see other reviews.) If a book retails for $25, he's going to sell it for $12.50. Even offering me just 10% of the price he intends to sell it for would be $1.25. But based on his offer of $25 for the full 75 books he's taking, he's offering me 33 cents. I understand that the second hand market is rough, but there is a fine line between justifiably making a lowball offer because it may take you some time to turn around the inventory and it's an unsure investment, and just trying to rip people of because you think that you can. THIRD EDIT!!! I went back to the store to pick up my books. I figured the process would be fairly easy. My friend parked by the sidewalk and I went in. I saw my bags, with about 1/4th of my books in them. So obviously Larry had separated my books and kept them that way. The woman that was there had no idea what was going on and said he would be back in a few minutes. Since I had my friend waiting in her car I was kind of peeved, but I said I would wait. After five minutes he wasn't back, and I asked her if she could call him to see how soon his return would be. "He doesn't have his cell phone." I told her I would have to leave and come back on the 26th, but just then Larry came in. I told him I was declining his offer and was just picking up my books. He gave me this look and said "Well look, how much were you looking for? Because I could maybe give you a little bit of a better offer..." but I told him no thank you, that I would just like to take back my books. Perturbed, he told me they were in a box on the floor, and I began unloading them back into my bags. I could feel him glaring holes into the back of my head, so when I was done I lifted up my bags and said "Thank you so much for the time you spent, have a good holiday!" He replied, in the smarmiest, bitchiest voice you can possibly imagine: "Yeah well. I *did* spend a lot of time. Like, an hour and a half." To which I replied, rather pointedly: "Well. That *is* the business you are in." And then I left... never to return.
label: NEG

text: Needless to say this is a good Korean restaurant since most of my Yelper friends had tried the food and contributed enough comments to the restaurant. Coty said it all so I won't repeat her precise descriptions. Instead, I will tell you something else. The restaurant changed hand one year ago. Now it is called 'One Family Korean Restaurant.' Don't panic! Nothing has changed. Food is still damn good. Service is still fast. Deco is still the same. Few reasons that I didn't give 5 star. First, The restaurant is hard to find. It tucked in behind a Korean Grocery store and not many English signs to indicate this place. If you drive east on W. Hillsborough Ave, it is on the right after you pass Henley road. If you drive by Golden Corral, you have just missed it. Second, customer groups this restaurant targeted at are mainly Asians, so their menu content offers no visual image to describe the dishes. If you are not familiar with Korean food, you are handicapped. It would be nice the owner make some adjustment to the menu to be more user friendly. The pictures on their website are nice though but without explain which dish it is. I admire people who carry on their traditions firmly like this restaurant. Food are as authentic as I had at Korea. It is difficult not to be Americanized when you run restaurant business. So I give them credit for preserve their traditions. I have few advices for those who are not familiar with Korean food but willing to try. Start with 'Seafood Pancake' (Haemul Pajeon). It is very good to share as appetizer. Then go for Grilled beef ribs (Gal Bi). It comes with 5 small vege/fish dishes, very traditional. Then stuff yourself with 'Dolsot Bibim bap', rice, meat, and vege cooked in a hot stone bowl. Make sure you add chili sauce on top and stir them well. Beside the seafood pancake, this is my favorite dish. In a cold winter night, it will fills the spot. My hubby love this restaurant. He had found his comfort food. We went there last Sunday night before 6pm. The place was half full. We plan to go back again this week. I will give more update later. BTW, we ordered 3 dishes, 4 beers and it costs 45 dollar including tax. This place is small but they can handle groups. I will suggest 6 people so everyone can share. It is very casual and because the nature of Korean food, you will smell like garlic and BBQ ribs later. So go casual. And Ladies, keep your dry clean only coats and fine leather bags home. You will thank me later.

text: Put shortly, this place is amazing. The food is phenomenal, the music is good and the atmosphere is exactly what you want from New Orleans. The interior feels like an old hole-in-the-wall carved out of a warehouse with wooden pillars supporting the roof and visible wood rafters. The lighting is bright enough to see your food, but dim enough to give it that great night club vibe. It's also all nonsmoking which is a huge plus for me. One word of caution, on busy nights, i.e., most of them, they give tables to people ordering food and people just getting drinks have to either sit at the bar or stand. Given that the food is so good, it's worth getting there a bit early and eating a plate or two so that you can enjoy the show at a table. In theory, you're still supposed to order food and drinks at the bar, but I found that the staff were always walking around and asking if you wanted anything else and were super friendly. So, I didn't ever need to actually order at the bar. The music we saw there was great and the venue is small enough that it's a great show no matter where you go. Luke Winslow-King was particularly amazing with his nearly-ragtime 40s style. He even brought an old 40s-era microphone that finished off the effect. The food here though is probably the most surprising. They have everything from goat cheese lamb sliders to tuna bulgogi and it's all good. My wife and I ate here twice and had six of the few dozen dishes with our favorites being the bulgogi rice bows and the lamb sliders. The feta fries were good, but about exactly what they sounded like: good french fries with cold feta crumbled over them. The sweet potato gnocchi were delicious, but the pork roast they came with didn't do very much for me. During happy hour they also have $4 really small plates. We had the beef empanadas which were delicious, and bacon-wrapped, cheddar-stuffed figs which sounded better than they were. Really, the only downside for me was that the drinks were only so-so. The tap selection consisted of 6 mostly local and light beers and as a self-admitted beer snob, I was a little disappointed, but liked the Brooklyn Octoberfest fine. The cocktail list wasn't exactly my cup of tea either, but they made a good cucumber-mint-lime virgin drink for my pregnant wife, so they were at least accommodating.

text: A good review shouldn't be difficult to write, but I just don't know where to start with Bluebeard. Every ounce of press Bluebeard has received is well deserved. Food we ordered: Starters: - Radishes, butter, salt: Simple, but ultimately kinda disappointing for one big reason: the butter was unsalted, which had no taste. We will try the pickle plate next time instead. - Oysters with watermelon mignonette: refreshing and delicious. Small plates: - Razor clams with garlic, lemon, parsley, and red pepper flakes: Wow. Razor clams of love. These rivaled the razor clams we had in Barcelona. Worth every penny. - Porchetta di testa with radish, caper, pea shoots, parsley, lemon: Good, fatty porchetta. Great flavor. Radishes were somewhat overpowering though, which was unexpected. Medium plates - Sardine Scapece, sweet peppers, mozzarella and grilled flat bread: Damn. Am I really in landlocked Indianapolis, Indiana? These really are quite like the fresh dishes I've had in Spain and Italy. - Pizza of beef tongue, romesco sauce, pickled peppers, oyster mushrooms, fromage blanc and arugula: This was right up there with the razor clams. Tongue wasn't chewy, romesco sauce was fantastic (one of my favorites) and the fromage blanc was fresh. Fantastic flavors. Dessert - Chess Pie with Peaches and cream: The waitress said she dreams about this pie, and for good reason. A healthy amount of sugar, butter and cream. Peaches had just the right about of tartness and firmness to balance out the rest (might have been a little too sweet for me otherwise). Service was great; wait staff is helpful in recommending if you're undecided. Atmosphere is one of my favorites: charming and comfortably up-scale, without being too fancy or fussy. The best part is, it's a direct reflection of the food you're about to eat. Great wine selection (available by the glass/quartino/bottle), awesome local brew on tap, and a fun and unique cocktail list just tops it off. And $10 for a round of beers for the kitchen? Absolutely. John and Abbi have a talent that they're passionate about, and I'm thankful they're sharing that talent with us! Thanks for a memorable dinner on a special night. We're looking forward to many more....

It all looks so generic - to the point where I question the quality of the chocolate used. The chocolates selection is nowhere near what Naked Chocolate offered, and certainly less unique in flavor and form. Half of the chocolate display is given up to stupid things I can make in my kitchen, like chocolate covered gummy bears, chocolate covered pretzels...not worth it AT ALL. Their pastry/baked goods display is also smaller, and not particularly appetizing. The candies you can buy boxed or bagged are all generic shiz you can buy for cheap anywhere else. This place seems like a rip-off, a scam to make you think they can make artisanal chocolates. And the staff? Half seemed miserable, and the other half looked like they were trying in vain to keep the smiles on their faces for customers. I like that they kept the general seating/layout of the place, but it is a little cramped if there were a line of customers ordering. text: I really hate to give this low of a rating, especially to a local area owned restaurant... I remembered the mixed reviews when the boy suggested we try it, I figured, I can always rely on the fish and chips... and I was starving. We decided on the full fish and chips platter ($11) and the sausage platter ($11) with the andoulie (spelling?) and "thirstingur" (?? started with a t) sausages, you get your choice of 2 from the 4. ). A friend got the shehards pie, as he had had it before ($12). We also wanted to try the cheese beer soup to start (Bowl is a little over $5). The cheese beer soup was good, but a bowl was too much for me, too potent maybe... the taste got old after a while for me... but I was sharing so it ended up being all eaten. The fish came out and I was surprised at the size and portions. It was probably 4 or 5 little fillets, which is fine I reasoned, b/c they batter them themselves. The first bite was actually good, I could taste the sweetness from the batter. The second and ever other bite afterwards, was like eating... air? Seriously NO flavor. The tartar sauce wasnt that great either. My fiance had to douse (spelling?) each bite of his with malt vinegar to add flavor. We were pretty dissappointed with this. I did think, I would rather have flavorless fish, than bad fish... so that is a plus. French fries or "chips" came with this, I got the garlic ones... I didnt taste any garlic... the most flavor on my plate come from the ranch that I dipped my fries in. The cucumber salad (a choice between that and a garden salad would be nicer) was also bland, I had our friend try it and he said it had no taste too... it was like water and cucumber. The sausages (which who knows which was which) were okay. One was really spicy, but juicy, the better of the two... and the other was really dry and not good. The mashed red potatoes were pretty good, and I ended up eating that all. I had a bite of the shepards pie, and realized why my friend stuck with that after we forced him to meet us here. I asked him if he had eaten here when he first got their and his answer implied he wasnt impressed before (b/c I asked if it wa good and there was a long pause) but since we chose it he would eat there... he had only eaten at the sparks location though. I just really dont want to risk coming back for such bland food. I didnt even finish my fish, I didnt see a reason why. I probably will try to try it again in the future, b/c its a local business and my fiance said that we didnt try the main attraction (the beer) yet. So who knows if it will be better on the next time. Also, the service was average. Coffee refills, one stop to check on us. Food was hot. I could tell she was busy, but we werent completely forgotton about, but we didnt really ask for much either.

text: This is a great desert biking trail. When I was visiting my Arizona people I rented a cannondale F400 hardtail from Cycle Tucson and headed out. It's not like mountain biking. It's mostly a pleasure ride, with ups and downs on rocky little hills, a few challenging gravel covered areas, desert plants and cactus all around. There are places on the trail that twist through dense patches of prickly pear cactus. As I was flying through there at full peddle I just hoped I wouldn't hit some loose sand and dive into it. Saw a mad cow with cactus needles sticking out of his nose glaring at me. It's an easy ride with some cool little shrines people set up along the trail. I rode around on multiple routes for 3 hours but you could spend a whole day there. I saw maybe 3 people the whole time. After that I rode back to my grandmas place on Pantano Wash. It's a fun ride, especially for a lazy amateur. Wear sunscreen and bring a camelback full of water.

The soup itself was passable, it wasn't horrible, but it sure wasn't the "wow" factor I was expecting from a designer soup joint. They didn't even give me enough soup to satisfy my hunger. Now let me tell you, it is a rare event that I leave any meal still feeling hungry and being forced to go somewhere else to top off the tank. I was pretty miffed that I had just spent so much money at Zoup and gotten so little in return. text: Overpriced considering the amount and quality of food you get for that price. Portrays itself a 'high-end' authentic Indian restaurant, which i don't feel it is, being a foodie and an Indian myself. Lacks flavor in most items served. Not thrilled with Laxmi's. We ordered a vegetarian platter as one of the starters, among others, because there were six of us there, so we figured we'd be able to try the different items on the plate. The plate arrived with one samosa cut into two, one aloo tikki cut into two and two pakoras, for $9, totally not worth it! We ordered chicken malabar ($8), a tiny breast of flattened chicken, battered with coconut and deep fried, enough for one person. For main course: mixed non-veg tandoori grille ($23), which looked and sizzled like it would be the best tasting dish on earth, but after tasting it, it was quite bland, enough to the point that my husband had to send it back to have some moreflavor added. They brought it back with some tikka masala sauce thrown over it, which now made it a curry instead of the tandoori grilled dish! I ordered Chicken Tikka Masala, which i must say was tasty, but, in the entire karai (serving bowl), there were barely 5-6 tiny little pieces of chicken and the rest of it was the curry which was gravy. At $14, again this item is not worth it. We also ordered Lamb Rogan Josh ($17) which was ok, Daal Makhani and Mutter Paneer ($12 which is high for small portions of veg dishes) tasted good. We also ordered a side of Raita. It came in a little saucer like container, which again was only enough for one person ($3). Since this place is BYO, we brought our own wine, which they did not help serve. But they charged a $5 corkage fee for opening and pouring it ourselves! Although the servers are polite, service is ok. They constantly forget to bring things and mistakes. Complimentary chutney & papadam these days is not a big deal. Most indian restaurants do that obligingly. We got one plate of a couple pieces of papadum, but since there were six of us, it was not enough for all of us, so we asked for more. We never got it. We used our Restaurant.com $25 voucher, but I think i would rather take me and my foodie guests somewhere else worth our while, our dollars and our palates.

text: This place was surprisingly good and a lot of fun. I was in Boise with family recently and we wanted to get some food. I spent a lot of time in Boise as a kid and it's not until you're much older you really start seeing the change and really start appreciating everything. Because of the local college, there is definitely a much younger demographic and a lot more interesting restaurants cropping up. Shige was just another one of the places, but its definitely one place that you have to try out if happen to find yourself in downtown Boise. Tucked away in a food complex of sorts, it takes some effort to find, or you'll miss it. Right on the strip that is N Main, this is one that should be at the top of your list. Very much like the style of Benihana, where the food is cooked right in front of you, Shige offers a bit more classier version of dining. With chairs all around the grill, this is the ideal place for a group to have some fun, watch the chef work his magic and have some delicious food. There is plenty of food to be had so be prepared to feast. Each meal comes with your choice of meat, veggies and/or seafood. Everything is cooked in sections, therefore you will be getting your veggies cooked, then your meat and finally your rice. The staff is very helpful and friendly, especially the chefs themselves. They were very pleasant, funny and were clearly enjoying their job. It created a great vibe and a fun dining experience. Surprisingly, Shige offered some really good sushi as well. Elaborate and somewhat intimidating, there are plenty of options to choose from. If you are in the crispy or soft mood, there is something for everyone. Shige is a great place to dine and have some solid Japanese food in the Boise area. If I find myself back in town, I will definitely be going again. Not only do you get some good food, you will have plenty of fun. I am glad I had to chance to experience this place.

It's also very clean and very fun. The basketball hoops are well attended by patrons, so you can always get a game in. The talent that shows up here is top notch, so there is not a lot of trash talk like at some other Indy parks. text: To me, this place is by far the best Japanese food in Tucson! Possibly in Arizona, since I haven't found a place in Phoenix that can equal its menu. Mind you, I didn't say best sushi. But I'll happily pay a little more for good food, so I'm not mad about it. My staples are usually either the salmon bento (teriaki or salted) or the seafood curry udon. I have yet to find another restaurant in Arizona that even attempts to make a curry udon, which really sucks because I fell in love with it back when I lived in Hawaii. All the main course soups etc come in a HUGE bowl, and I've never had a problem with them skimping on the protein. The seafood curry udon has salmon, scallops, shrimp and squid, plus the usual cabbage, carrots and sweet potatoes. if i'm extra hungry I'll order double the noodles, for only $1.25 or so extra. The curry broth is damn near perfect, and reminds me of the curry udon I used to get in Hawaii. The bento boxes are great. They come with grilled sweet potatoes, seaweed salad, regular salad, rice and the main course. You have your choice of rice, either plain white or the Japanese rice that has all the seasonings in it (I can't remember what it's called off the the top of my head right now). I've never had a bad meal there and anyone I've ever brought with me has always enjoyed their food. The ambiance is great with all the retro Japanese anime toys and figurines all around the walls, and the gift shop where you can buy chopsticks, mochi, and other Japanese knick knacks and doodads. It's original and eccelctic and i think it definitely deserves the Best Japanese Food in Tucson title.

text: My wife and I went to Otto's last night for dinner, and it was excellent German food. We just moved to this area in June and I've been passing this place by all the time and always wondered what the food and beer selection was like. It was great! Now it's not gourmet food by any means, but it's great food for cold winter nights. We met up with some of my in-laws at the bar, the tap selection was impressive and they had a little bit of everything, it's kind of hard not to have a good beer with 23 taps. The bartender was friendly and helpful with letting me try out a beer I had never heard of before. We took our drinks to our table and looked over our menus. Our group decided to go only German and not get any of the non-German offerings. We ordered the Rauchfleisch and Potato Pancakes for our appetizers. The Rauchfleisch was more or less us just being adventurous and trying something new. It was good but probably something none of us would order again. The Potato Pancakes on the other hand were great and definitely something we'll order again. My wife and mother-in-law tried the Snapper Soup, and both were raving about it. My Chicken Orzo soup was definitely homemade and tasted good. Our entrees that we ordered were the Jaeger Schnitzel, Schweinepfeffer, Neuschwanstein and the Sausage Sampler. The only complaint with entrees was with my brother-in-laws order, the Jaeger Schnitzel. It wasn't because of the taste but rather the portion size. He seemed quite happy with it after tasting it though and plowed through it. My Sausage Sampler was fantatstic and anybody who loves German Sausages should be all over this one. I had this with their amazing sauerkraut and spaetzle with gravy. The Bratwurst was my favorite with the Hungarian Brat following a close second. Our finale was the German Chocolate Cake, and it was a let down. After all that great German food the cake ended up being stale with not enough of the caramel coconut that was the best part of it. Overall though the food was great and we'll be heading back there again. We're looking forward to trying the outside seating when the weather gets warmer out. For the beer people out there I found two great beers here. The Bavarian Barbarian (which is not listed on the menu and may be a seasonal) and the Hofbrau Dunkel. Two dark beers with great flavor.

text: I wish I could give zero stars. First of all, you have to pay to get into the casino. $10 a person for 24 hours. They give you a $10 gift card that you have to use for something other than gambling. This is how they get you into their restaurants or or store or to pay at the bar. The machines are terrible and so are the table games. We spent $230 and didn't earn one point to get the $10 free on our cards. You only need one point and neither of us earned a single point. This is ridiculous. We will never come back and they ought to be ashamed. I understand this is part of a law, but we will never return to ANY casino in Pennsylvania because of this.

Though I found books I was interested in, I just couldn't support this guy. Helpful hint, if you want money, be mindful of who you might be offending. Dinner party rules apply in retail.

text: Been to cabinet many times including bringing all my friends for a birthday trip. Although I have never eaten here it really is in my top 5 bars in the city without a doubt. They debuted their spring cocktail list inspired by herbs and garden last night and I had the pleasure of drinking their basil cocktail. Wish i could do it more justice but I know it was headlined by pisco and was spot on and perfect. They always have a rotating cocktail featured list created by different inspirations. I remember once it was based on a tom waits album another by Shakespearean plays. Staff is always so knowledgeable especially the bartenders (bill and Giuseppe fucking rule). The beers are from all over including their own brews which are pretty cool. Go on thursdays and you can find drew nugent and his band playing some great songs and you feel like your in a boardwalk empire episode and not washington square. coolest bar ive been to in a long time.
label: POS

text: This is easily the worst buffet of all the major casinos on all of Reno. We had the brunch today (Sunday) and it cost $12.99 per person. The food was terrible and the selection was worse. Additionally, it seemed like they had no clue as to how to run a buffet. They had mashed potatoes and no gravy. They had a small mexican food section with no tortillas. The "carvery" had only ham (it was dry) and they had 2 kinds of horseradish to serve with it. Someone needs to tell them that horseradish is normally served with prime rib, not ham. For $12.99, you can get a much better meal at any of the other casino buffets, and that is including Circus Circus, which is cheaper. Don't waste your money here. You will be highly disappointed.
label: NEG

text: You can't go wrong with Bazbeaux's Pizza. It's a must if you live or just visiting Indy. I believe they have 3 locations. Downtown, Broad Ripple and Carmel. This visit was to Broad Ripple. The pizza is always amazing with eclectic twist to the atmosphere. They have specialty pizza and create your own. I selected the Bazbeaux special and added prosiecutto. Went with the thin and wheat crust. The wheat crust has a better flavor then the regular crust. Bazbeaux's is always one of the top pizza places to eat in Indy. They also have a lot of different beers you won't find in most pizza joints. Outstanding!
label: POS

text: It was time for the office Christmas lunch again and I happened to pass a giant billboard advertising the new Chop. Who can resist a 10 foot steak? I put the thought into the bosses' heads and we made a reservation for an 11:30 lunch on a Friday. By the time my coworker and I got to the restaurant, a few of our bosses were a few sangrias in (cheap sangria on Friday...highly, highly recommend the white wine sangria...freaking delicious). We all split an appetizer tray with bacon chicken wings (SO good), spicy peas, steak bites and some kind of cheese toast. I went for the top sirloin as a main, with wasabi infused mashed potatoes and vegetables. The potatoes were good, but I didn't really taste the whole wasabi thing. Good mashed potatoes, but nothing special. The steak....ohhhh the steak was unbelievable. Cooked to the perfect medium rare, tender, juicy...oh I'm getting hungry again. Their dessert menu is seriously tempting, and I got the sampler which had a slice of chocolate cake (meh..it was chocolate cake), a mini raspberry crème brulée (pretty tasty) and the pièce de résistance...a small slice of their carribean rum cake. If nothing else, PLEASE go to Chop to get this cake. It is the best rum cake I've ever had. It was rum-y and cinnamon-y and coconut-y and everything good in the world-y. Service was excellent. The waitress was friendly, chatty when appropriate, good at recommendations, helpful and very prompt and attentive. The prices are fairly cha-ching but I left seriously satisfied (and I wasn't paying anyways, so who cares). The restaurant got very, very busy so I would suggest reservations if you're planning on trying it out. And you really should. Go now. Seriously.
label: POS

text: I had been meaning to visit for many months and now wish that I had earlier! I first visited about a month ago, but since have been back every several days. I have tried a variety of caffeinated drinks (I have had no alcohol there, but their selection is good), several baked goods, and sweets. I have been thoroughly impressed with the service, ambiance, drinks, and food. It is small so it is difficult to spread out, but I like that kind of comfortableness. The artwork is fun and different. The seating varies from hard wooden and metal chairs to deep, comfy sofas. I really appreciate that their quiches have thus far been vegetarian. I have also had some good conversations and met some really cool people there. So much for my rambles; I hope it helps.
label: POS

text: YUMMY!!! SO DELICIOUS!!!! The scrumptious, large buttery cookies were satisfying. I purchased a few cookies to bring home, but I broke off pieces to try. As a result, no whole cookies made their home. I think the chocolate chip cookie was the best. The chocolate chip dipped chocolate cookie was good, but it was a little TOO sweet. Overall, you can't go wrong here.
label: POS

text: We're regular visitors to Santa Barbara as we have family we enjoy visiting. Once our children were born, we found it necessary to find lodging for the longer weekends. So, we regularly try to find good deals when we go up. The $100 we spent for a two double bed room was a price we couldn't pass up. At that amount, I'd normally be a lot more lenient with an establishment. The accommodations were dated and spartan. But the TV worked, the shower had hot water and the bed kept us comfortable for the few hours we were there. The bathroom had an awkward design where you couldn't reach the toilet without closing the door. They offered a continental breakfast which made the $100 even more a bargain. The room was smartly decorated as a 50s diner and the food was fresh. My chief complaint was the lack of heat in the room. Our heater obviously broke during the evening and management wasn't willing to discount for our inconvenience. I didn't expect a free night, but certainly something to acknowledge that we had to sleep in a ~45 deg room. Given the opportunity to get much better accommodations for a few dollars more, I'd likely never stay here again.
label: NEG

text: I was really craving a blooming onion, so my mom and I went to this location to get one. I was pretty disappointed. It was probably what I should've expected. It wasn't consistent really, being very soft in some parts and too crispy at others. I also ordered a chicken and swiss sandwich that came with lettuce, tomato, and bacon. it wasn't bad, but not great. Our waitress was attentive, fast and patient. I'm probably not going back.
label: NEG

text: Finally got a chance to try Sushime tonight. I'll always welcome more good sushi options in town. We had the following: Shrimp Tempura Roll - yes, it's tame... but it's also one of the best I've ever tasted Spicy Scallop Roll - slightly above average Ocean Roll - this was odd... the picture looks nothing like the description and the actual roll was like the picture, not the description. mixture of tuna, yellowtail and some others... very clean and fresh with lots of fish... recommended Eel Diablo Roll - I love unagi, and this roll delivered.. the tempura asparagus in the center really complimented everything White Snake Roll - "Is This Love?" No, sadly it was average at best... kinda disappointed, and I think David Coverdale would be too The presentation was great. Rivals some of the most expensive and trendy sushi spots I've been to around the country. Prices were average for Nashville, but the portions were great. Not too much rice, which is good. Also had a full Japanese menu. I'll have to try it sometime. Glad this place is just down the street. The bad (if I have to be picky): The ginger wasn't that good. No low sodium soy option. The chairs are not comfortable... this place needs more booths.
label: POS

text: This is a 'quantity' over 'quality' restaurant--lots of food for the $ but wasn't very good. Our server was also very bland--not friendly at all and only returned to our table when it was necessary for him...not us. We will not be returning.
label: NEG

text: This was my 2nd time visiting Branzino and was shocked at the difference in quality of food and service this time around We had an 8pm reservation on a gorgeous Saturday night so chose to sit in the huge courtyard out back to enjoy the weather. We were promptly greeted by our waiter who filled up our water glasses and wine - which is about the best service we recieved all night (or more accurately, the only service we recieved all night). The waiter came back once more to take our order and we never saw him again. Our appetizers were dropped off at the table, without our empty wine glasses being refilled from our bottle which was sitting about 5 feet away from us. I dont recall the exact dishes we ordered, but I do remember the grilled squid was delicious and perfectly cooked. I got up from our table to grab our bottle of wine (since we were now out of water as well) and filled our glasses. Two waiters walked by me, not one offered to do this. Our entrees came, and unfortunately, mine was pretty subpar. I ordered the Tagiatelle Nero (Squid Ink pasta with Shrimp, Sea scallops, and roasted peppers in a garlic marinara) I had one scallop in the entire dish and 2 shrimp....for $19. I found the taste of the red peppers to be overwhelming and took away from the flavor of the spicy marinara and squid ink pasta. I would have mentioned this to a server, if they bothered to come around after our food was dropped off to ask if everything was ok. We had a double bottle of wine, which my husband and I had to get up from the table to get and refill ourselves the entire evening. I probably couldve looked passed the mediocre food that evening if the service had been anywhere near decent.
label: NEG

text: On Feb 11, 2012 I bought a couch here. They said it would take 8 weeks since it was a special order. Fast forward to April 11, and there is no sign of our couch. Their order tracking system is PATHETIC since they couldn't even tell me where our couch was in the process without calling the factory. Now on April 26th, apparently the couch is made and at a warehouse, but won't get shipped to the store until there is a full truck which might be around May 10th. It would take the store about 3 days to schedule a delivery making the order 12 weeks. It seems that custom orders ALWAYS take 12 weeks according to sales person. This wasn't the time frame told to me by the salesman. The receipt I was given says approximately 8 to ___ weeks. There is no 12 on the receipt. It seems that 12 weeks being 150% longer than the original quoted time frame is still "approximately 8 weeks". I think I need to go down and demand 50% of my money back. That would mean I still paid approximately the sticker price according to their math. If you go to Kane's and they tell you your furniture will only take 8 weeks, they are lying to you. I have no idea if or when I will actually get my sofa and continue to use my patio furniture in the living room. There are plenty of other furniture stores on 34th which will happily take your money and deliver product to you in a timely manner. I will NEVER buy anything from Kane's again, and I would recommend to anyone looking for furniture to skip this establishment.
label: NEG

text: On new years day trios was the only place open in the area. I should have gone for a hot dog at the 7-11 this was truly one of the worst pizzas I have ever tasted. They don't sell slices so ended up buying 3 small pies at 15.00 each which is outrageous, we had to explained to the kid behind the register that we wanted a real tomato pie, it seems they call every pizza there a tomato pie which is not the case at all. Avoid this place at all cost. If you want good thin crust pizza go to Jules or trevi and of course there is always good old pizza box. I would go to dominos before ever going to trios again. Wish yelp would allow zero stars as one star is too generous

text: Truth be told we haven't stayed there. HOWEVER, If I could give negative stars for customer service I would. Just dealt with Daniel the manager who didn't seem interested in dealing with my situation. Tried to schedule a night to redeem an older gift card that had no expiration date. This card was purchased when it was a bed and breakfast. There was no mention of the card being invalid if the ownership changed. Well, you guess it! Daniel's final negative response was that I should call "The Better Business Bureau." He had no regrets and no options for us. I think he has a long way to go when dealing with customers.

text: I went here for lunch today having heard a lot of good things about this place, but I have to say I was really disappointed. My biggest complaints with Seoul Taco have to be the slow service and poor organization; I got there a little before 1pm and there was maybe a 8-10 person line but it took FOREVER (well, 45 minutes, but still) until I even got to place my order. To make matters worse, they ran out of gochujang (amazing hot sauce which is one of my favorite parts of Korean cuisine), eggs, veggies AND bulgogi, so by the time it was my turn to order my choices were pretty limited. One lady before me had ordered the bulgogi bowl, but since they ran out of everything all she got was meat and lettuce. Not very appetizing. The food is not bad; I got spicy pork and chicken tacos (I couldn't have ordered much else with their ingredient shortage), both of which were pretty good and fairly priced. Bottom Line: The food is good, but the service time and running out of that many ingredients is unacceptable.
label: NEG

text: After a hot afternoon, with driving all over Tucson, I stopped by BTO for the first time to check it out. It was pretty nice inside and the ladies at the registers greeted me in a friendly manner. There were a number of options in yogurt flavor (but it's nothing compared to Cold Stone). The seating in the place doesn't look too comfy and the tables are a little small but the place is affordable. I liked the many fruit varieties offered with the toppings section (This makes me feel less guilty on my diet...hehehe.) You can test flavors with little cups they offer which was nice. Overall I like the place and will stop by when I'm in the neighborhood.

text: We came in to have a good time drinking and singing on a Sunday night with karaoke in mind. The pitchers of beers were cheap and the service was good but the karaoke was mediocre. The microphones kept screetching because they were set up to close to the speakers and the TV screen was angled where you couldn't really read and sing at the same time. This place requires you to stumble in with your beer goggles in order to find it appealing. Not sure I would have even enjoyed the experience slightly if it weren't for my company.
label: NEG

text: They really nailed it! The food and service were simply perfect. We felt attended to, without being bothered. Zeke and Carter and the rest of the front of the house were warm, kind, and really helped us to feel celebrated on our anniversary. And the food... A stunning 7 courses all paired with wine that showcased local ingredients and a LOT of creativity. My favorite was the squash blossom stuffed with corn pudding, served on a basil aioli and roasted heirloom tomates. It was cooked perfectly. It is so rare (as a professional cook myself) that I am blown away by a dish, but this really was a little taste of perfection. The wine selections were thoughtful and fun. A fabulous evening! Well done August!
label: POS

text: Wow, I'm reading the glowing reviews here and am surprised to see that more people weren't subjected to the rude, downright terrible service that I received at my first (and last) visit to this shop. I'm a newbie to cheese, and still discovering what I'm into. I live a street over from this place, and I've passed by here many times. The other day, I decided to finally stop in. I should have known it was a bad sign when one of the shopkeepers completely overlooked me to attend to someone who'd walked in at least five minutes after I did, although I'd obviously been waiting longer. When he finally decided to acknowledge me (didn't catch his name, but he's a tall, slim man, probably early 30's, with longish dark hair that's slightly wavy), I asked him for suggestions on different cheeses to try. He kept asking "what do you like?" While I couldn't name any particular types of cheese (as I said, I'm a complete novice cheeses and I informed him of that), I tried my best to describe the texture and flavor I preferred, and he made no attempt to hide his impatience with me. After I'd decided on a cheese (or settled, I should say, I didn't want to continue to "inconvenience" this guy), I told him I was going to grab one more item and check out (took all of 20 seconds as I knew what I wanted). When I returned, he was busily chatting it up with other customers. I gave him the item and told him I was ready to pay, he placed it behind the counter and continued to chat with other customers. I should have taken this opportunity to leave, but I was really so shocked at how rude and disrespectful his behavior was, I just stood there, flabbergasted. Finally, another attendant noticed I'd been standing there, and rang up my order. To be fair, the other attendants seemed very friendly, and I should have worked with one of them instead of the surly, condescending fellow I ended up with. His personality made him better suited to work at a hotdog stand or food cart, not an upscale (and rather pricey) specialty grocer. Apparently, my business wasn't wanted here, and I'll gladly take it elsewhere.
label: NEG

text: We choose to eat here because it was Fiesta days in Santa Barbara and every place was packed with rowdy people drinking. Since we had our children we definitely wanted somewhere more mellow. This seemed like the perfect fit. The food was fabulous everyone enjoyed their food but the problem with the food was the portions were so small we all ended up still very much hungry afterwards. The service was just about the worst I have ever had. Our waitress was practically non existent and we had to ask her every time we needed anything. She never came to check on us and eventually one of the other waitresses noticed and came to our table several times. On our way out we noticed our waitress just sitting at the bar. Apparently serving is not her forte. Anyway bottom line is bad service and overpriced small portioned food. Avoid this place.

text: Nice relaxed atmosphere, fried Alligator is good. Three stars, because it took 30 mins for the appetizer to come out, and 45 mins for the main dishes. Most of the food we ordered are all fried, it should take no more than 20 mins to serve. I can only imagine how long it will take on a busy game day. If your hungry go eat somewhere else first then come here, if your thirsty and want to snack on some good seafood! Then this is the place for you. Edit: Took off another star I came back here on Friday night 8/3/12, I just wanted to get some drinks before I fly back to Los Angeles. I tried to get in by the open bar patio area and two rude wanna be bouncers are charging $15 bucks to get in to watch some crappy band. I said no thanks, I mean you can get in the Viper Room in Los Angeles for cheaper than that and watch a really good band.
label: NEG

text: I have found my new favorite restaurant! La Calaca Feliz was highly recommended by a foodie friend. Boy was she on target! The interior has the beautiful bones of the previous restaurant with an elegant Mexican flair. Service was very friendly and welcoming. Nice to hear servers present Mexican food with a Spanish lilt in their voice. Hubby & I tried 4 appetizers - the meatballs, pulpo, chorizo & duck. Meatballs were perfectly cooked, with cheese in the middle. These had a nice full flavor that did not get lost in the mourh. Pulpo was nicely seasoned and pleasant. The chorizo we fought over and sent a clean plate back to the kitchen. They are served with a tortilla and frankly, I'll have to order them again to figure out what is in there in addition to the chorizo and beans. The duck - well , we had it after the chorizo so frankly I don't remember. Each plate was unique and so good we'd have ordered 2 of each, but that would have meant another hour on the treadmill. I definitely will be back. So glad it is in the neighborhood so we don't have to deal with the weekend crowds other reviewers are struggling with. But what the heck, a few margaritas even the whiners may relax and enjoy the night!
label: POS

text: Based off the Neely's recommendation of the 'best thing we ever ate', we stopped at Raz'z last month while in Nashville. It's a unique sort of place in that the inside of the restaurant is extremely dark looking with little lighting and to be honest, a little depressing and cookie cutter. Fortunately for us, we sat outside on the patio and it was very warm and inviting. The wait staff was great and very attentive. Chef Raz was also walking around and thanking people for coming in. It was a nice touch. My husband and I both started with the standard house salad and house dressing. Both were surprisingly very good. The salad was more than the usual lettuce and cucumbers. It also had Diced Tomatoes, Cheddar and Jack Cheeses, Bacon, and Sliced Egg. I then got the highly recommended Jambalaya Pasta with half rice and half pasta. I would get the all rice next time b/c it was more tasty that way. I'll agree with everyone that it is a great dish - maybe not the best I ever ate, but definitely a dish to recommend. My husband got the Shrimp and Crawfish Ettoufe - which he liked but had hoped it would be a little more spicy. I would recommend the place to others b/c I thought the food was good and the wait staff was great.
label: POS

text: I am not a huge seafood fan, but this place was very nice. They had a wide selection of seafood and appetizers as well as a pretty extensive wine list. The atmosphere was great and since we were a party of 6, we got a private table surrounded by wooden partitions and it seemed like we had the place to ourselves! Being in Rittenhouse Square, it was pretty pricey, but I wasn't footing the bill. The deserts were awesome, I had the sorbet trio and the lime-mint sorbet was AMAZING. Try it. Seriously.

Last visit left waitress cash tip and marked out tip on card receipt and she decided to fill it in anyway and change the total. Called to complain and manager offered a refund which never came. Sloppy management, bad staff. Won't be going back

text: We continue to be thrilled that PPHV is in business here in Philly. Jared and his crew truly get it. Our boy has stayed here a whole bunch of times now, and we never have any reservations that he will be well taken care of. Thank you PPHV for doing such a great job.

text: So unimpressed. Soggy fries. Flavorless burger. Expensive, to boot. I get that some people really care about grass-fed organic blah blah. But this is a burger. Come on. I will not be returning. I would suggest going to Five Guys or Lucky's Last Chance if you're craving a flavorful, juicy burger.
label: NEG

text: I'm not a huge fan of Mexican food, but I do enjoy a good taco. In my admittedly limited opinion, El Jarocho has the best in the City. Their steak tacos are excellent, forcing me to make a weekly trek down there despite the fact that I live in University City. I've tried the Mexican Burrito once, and while it was ok, I just can't help ordering the steak tacos with a Mexican Coke and flan for desert every time. Aside from that, the chips with the pinkish/orange dip is a great combination. Another positive: the place is BYOB, so you can come in with a six pack of Modelo Especial or a bottle of Cuervo if you so desire. On the downside, they have one waitress who doesn't speak English especially well and tends to mess up my order slightly (I always get my steak tacos without onions). Now that I know what a "cebolla" is I don't think that will be a problem anymore.
label: POS

text: This is this best place for really decent and quick Mexican food. Really good for the price if you are on a budget.

text: Not that great for sushi. All rolls taste similar. Somebody recommended this place to us and I was disappointed. For the best sushi try Simple sushi in Nampa. It is by far the best sushi around!!!

The wait was too long so I went back the next night at 5:30. This time, they had chicken, but they were out of cornbread and the three sides I ordered were not ready -- another 30 minutes. I left empty handed, again. Maybe the next time I'll stop in when they open; that might be the only chance you have to try the food.

To add to it, they charged me 80 bucks... I can see a thread coming loose, but added stains to a silk dress? Such a bummer.

text: This should have been a special-occasion dinner, rather than a normal night out because of the unforgettable meal we had (with an unforgettable price tag). From beginning to end, it was a perfect experience, from the staff to the courses to the goody bag (and menu) they sent us home with at the end of the night. You have no choice but to do the tasting menu, and we added the wine with it, too, which only made the night better. We had the table for the night and were told we could ask for more of anything we loved. Vetri made me love things I always thought I hated (foie gras, ramps). The almond ravioli were memorable, and the spinach gnocchi was amazing. THe beet sorbet was suprisingly good. I loved that they served each of us different dishes for each course so we could try each other's meals. My only complaint was that there was so much food and so many courses, that after a while I didn't really want to eat any more.
label: POS

text: Been there only once but I enjoyed it. All vegetarian! A small cafeteria-style place. All-You-Can-Eat. You pay first, get your food, find a table, and enjoy...and get some more food. Selections are salad with lots of fixings and a few different dressings. A couple of main entrees, sides, and a dessert. Loved the strawberry havalah...actually it was my favorite part of the meal. I think their menu changes weekly so make sure to check their website. The only downfall was the chai tea, too diluted for my taste. I would definitely go back for a kick-back peaceful vegetarian meal any day when I'm visiting Tucson.
label: POS

text: I want to love Patrick's, the owner is very nice, the location is great-now on Main street in Zionsville-but the food is mediocre at best. I have heard the Owner say it was a dream to move to the current location, why go to all the trouble to serve such average food? Such a waste to be in this premier spot and not do a better job with the cuisine. They need a new chef -which hopefully would bring a more appealing presentation of the dishes when brought to the table-and to retrain the staff-my waiter was very friendly but took forever to get us our drinks, never brought water, didn't come to check on us but rushed us thru dessert because we were nearing closing time. The second star is for the location, go there for a drink but eat somewhere else.
label: NEG

text: If you beat the crowd you're in. Small but that's the only negative. Everything I've tried on the menu is AMAZING! They even have vegetarian/vegan items. I always get whatever french toast special they have. I always take people who stay with me for Mardi Gras here for breakfast before we hit the parades.
label: POS

text: I have never written a review, good or bad, about a restaurant before. Nor do I anticipate doing so in the future. However, I felt compelled to do so after last night to help people avoid making the same mistake as I. We went here after reading a number of good reviews, and foolishly disregarding the bad ones. I have to believe that the good reviewers were writing about a different restaurant. As we walked to our table I saw many of the other patrons drinking the free margaritas that everyone keeps writing about. This was a good sign to me because a recurring complaint in the bad reviews was the lack of this concoction. Our waiter came over, explained the specials and poured us our water. I thought to myself, her it comes, FREE MARGARITA! Nope, no margarita, in fact, he didn't even bring us glasses for the beverages we brought with us until he decided to mosey on over and ask if we wanted to order. We finally ordered and started with an appetizer special and chips and salsa. I don't want to sound cheap, but if I'm paying six bucks for chips and salsa it better be spectacular. We received a basket of chips accompanied by three dishes of accoutrements. Dish one contained a brownish liquid. Dish two contained a pickled jalapeno sliced in half. Dish three contained a standard type salsa. Brown liquid was not good, in fact it was disgusting. Jalapenos were tasty, but how do you put that on a chip? "Standard" salsa, good, really good. Buuuuut, I forgot to mention that for your six dollars you got about a quarter cup of it so it was gone in a few minutes leaving us with a six dollar basket of chips. The appetizer special was good. That is the last time I will use that word in this review. Moving on. For entrees I ordered a chicken dish and my girlfriend ordered quesadillas and crispy taco appetizers for her meal. text: Being a mom and also working full-time, with a full-time employed husband, we don't have tons of time or energy to devote to cooking. Frankly, we spend far too much money (and calories) on eating out, just because we don't have the inclination to plan ahead meals while grocery shopping. For all those reasons, we decided to give Dream Dinners a shot. Cost savings are arguable... if I was a coupon junkie, plan-ahead-meal, person, there's no doubt it would be cheaper to grocery shop if you were organized enough (and had the time). But for folks who just go to the store and buy a bunch of stuff, and don't really plan ahead, and don't bother to do much with coupons, this way is cheaper. Cheaper. But not cheap. We signed up for the intro special of "18 servings". The intro special also includes a free 3-serving dinner entree as well, so a total of 21 "servings" for about $75. We did the 3-serving meals, so we got a total of 7 meals. You can do either 3-serving or 6-serving portions. Since it's just the two of us, we did all 3-serving portions. We sampled a variety of dishes, including a build-your-own calzone, BBQ shrimp on skewers, and a bacon tortellini. The assembly process itself is quite easy. No need to be intimated by complicated steps or confusing measurements. All the steps are clearly outlined and measurements are made fool-proof. My husband and I agreed this was a great project for folks who aren't great with cooking, and will help one build confidence with their culinary skills. Once you've made all your meals, you slap directions already printed out on stickers on to the plastic bag where you put all the items for baking that dish. Then you take it home and stick it in the freezer. Voila! The food itself is good, at least what we've had so far. The shrimp and calzone were a little bland, so we'll try to spice dishes up a bit next time we prepare. It's not the most delicious food, but it tastes homecooked (and is easy to prepare). Next month, we're doing the standard minimum order of 36 servings (so that's 12 3-serving meals), and spent about $140 in advance. It's a little less than $12 a meal. What gets 5-stars is the service! The husband-and-wife team who run the place are an adorable older couple who couldn't have been sweeter or more helpful. I think we'll be regulars... so if you happen in on a Saturday morning and see me, please say hello!

text: First, the good: the server was incredibly friendly and helpful. The niceties end there, sadly. I came here two days in a row; the first for a mid-bikeride snack (potato wedges and kefta) and the second for a normal lunch. I'm going to go dish by dish to make sure I don't miss any of the misery. Potato Wedges (Tz'iips) These were fine, albeit unsalted; however it's hard to mess fried potatoes up. Kefta Dry, flavorless rice with tiny little vegan meatballs. The meatballs had a decent flavor but there were only three of them. I paid $7.50 for three tiny turd-looking things and some dry basmati. Disappointing, but not so much that we didn't give them a second chance. Mujadera This was the reason we came. A layered dish of rice, spicy lentils, and caramelized onions? I could practically taste the rich, oily goodness. What did we get? Possibly the saddest dish I've had all year. The rice was dry like in the kefta, the lentils were dry and crumbly with almost no flavor, and the onions were NOT caramelized and barely even onions: they were dehydrated shallots. Crunchy and dry like bits of parchment. I literally had to put the ketchup from my potatoes on the onions to choke them down. Upon first glance my dining partner thought they were some bizarre wood chip garnish. How can a chef get away with that? Just so we're on the same page, caramelized onions are sliced onions slow-cooked over low heat with lots of nommy fat. The end result is something soft, rich and luxurious. This was paper. I cannot believe the menu lies in this way. Garlic Hummus and Bessara with Pita The pita tasted like it had been frozen and heated up in a microwave. incredibly tough and unpleasant. The hummus was unsalted. I'm barely a cook but I have no idea how one can make hummus without salt. The bessara just tasted like spicy cumin. Sign me up for Sabra any day over what Meze offers. Shawarma This was just an embarrassment to vegans and vegetarians. Totally flavorless. I was forced to employ my ketchup once again to make it palatable. It was the same tough-as-rubber pita stuffed with shredded cabbage and some tomatoes in what tasted like diluted vegenaise. The veggie chicken inside was fine (we confirmed it was not made on site: what a surprise!) but tasted better dipped in ketchup like a child's chicken mcnugget than in the pathetic vegenaise sauce. I don't know what is up with this place; is there just nothing else veg-friendly in st. petersburg? This was some of the worst food I've ever eaten. Perhaps the vegetarian dishes hide behind dairy and eggs and have something approximating flavor but the vegan "highlights" we tried were just awful. Do not go here.

I even tried to salvage the filet mignon, but it was dry and flavorless, nor could I find something in my own fridge to make it edible. I'm really disappointed in the sandwich as everyone on yelp has good reviews, not to mention the fact that I'm still hungry. Perhaps I should try dine-in and see how that turns out. Additionally, I also ordered the creamed spinach and cornbread pudding. The sides were good, the spinach a little too peppery for my taste, but both creamy and spinach-y. Prices were a little higher than normal for Vietnamese restaurants, but for an extra couple bucks for the pho, you get a much nicer atmosphere and friendlier service than at Kien Giang.
