text: I visited the Quincy Street Bistro on 6/4 as part of a group of 3 people. We had gotten reviews from a friend who knows one of the owners and was familiar with all the work they had done to fix up the building. They have parking across the street, which is convenient but not the easiest to cross the street. We got there and the place was pretty full and loud. The bar looks pretty nice, but the street-level floor has very little on the walls and no carpet, making for the noise level to be so high that the three of us had a hard time even talking to each other. We sat in a small back room and it was even louder back there, probably because there were a few tables with large, loud groups, but the building and room decor (or lack thereof) just didn't help it. I was suprised at how large their menu is. However, for a "bistro", and for something described as a "Gastropub" or casual "new American", the menu seemed more like south St. Louis run of the mill bar and grill. Although there were many options on the menu, nothing screams culinary creativity or unique "American" food For starters, we had an order of the Tavern Chips with horseradish sauce. The sauce was pretty good, but the chips were cut too thick and were soggy, oily and tasted like wet cardboard dipped in oil. If you didn't smear them on the sauce, they were barely edible. For food, we ordered a few different sandwiches. We skipped the meatloaf, although I was thinking it would be a twist on the classic, the description was too honest to really make it attractive (seasoned ground beef baked with ketchup). My friend started with the Quincy Street Monster dog - a half pound hot dog served deep fried. He said it was good, but that it tasted exactly like you'd expect a generic deep fried giant hotdog to taste. Other than size, there was nothing special about this "Monster Dog". My other friend ordered the chicken fried steak and was thoroughly disappointed. It was too dry, bland... and looked like something out of a TV dinner box. I had a cajun burger, cooked "medium". It was described on the menu as "dredged" in blackening spices, but in reality this was a decent sized tasteless hunk of hamburger. I really could not taste the spices, and the Pepper Jack cheese did not help the sandwich. The burger was served with fries (although cottage cheese was an option too), and the fries were decent - salty, skinny fries - somewhat reminiscent of steak n' shake fries. Their iced tea did not taste freshly brewed - I think it may have been a mix. Overall, I was disappointed and will not be back. There were a few positives about the meal - the servers were very nice and attentive, the portions were very generous, and we didn't have to wait too long for our food. I really hope this place makes it - it is good to have these sort of businesses in the neighborhood and the owners obviously put a lot into rehabbing the building, but the location will not make up for the mediocrity of the bar-grill food.

text: After an especially hot and steamy viewing of Showgirls and a quick flip through the spring Victoria's Secret catalogue, I was in the mood for more cheap thrills. As my dedicated readers know, I have a debilitating fear of birds, and believe touching their bones allows the bird's soul to torment me in the afterlife, so I generally stick to boneless wings. There I was, lounging sideways in my booth with my legs crossed, taking my first bite of a buffalo wing through my Mexican wrestler facemask with a manic look in my eyes, content with all in the world and expecting nothing but the best from the chefs at Hooters. What the sauce lacked for in quality it made up for in butter. However, the meat itself was like a dry piece of roadkill cartilage sprayed with the foam they use to seal cracks in your basement walls. And I know, having eaten my share of roadkill in my many trips to Nigeria to complete business deals with dying diamond mine heiresses. I asked for more wings after dumping the remaining 9 1/2 wings on my plate on the floor under my table, and elected to go with the teriyaki wings. They had a corporate tang, a hint of mild depression - a charity-dinner appetizer made for 200 people in a sleezy Bangkok convention center. Needless to say, I dumped those as well, this time using my foot to discreetly push the growing graveyard of wasted chicken lives further under the table while coughing and waving at the hostess standing by the door to cover my movements. I decided to take my final order to go, and because they apparently don't allow that on the all-you-can-eat option, I was forced to stick all 5 parmesan garlic wings in the pocket of my slacks. I give 1 star for the wrestling promotion and the lovely Mexican wrestling mask (I plan to wear it often at home), and 1 additional star because I caught a 4 pound large-mouthed bass the next day when I used the parmesan garlic wings as bait. text: The Brick House is average, no more and no less. The property is an old converted bank. A pretty cool space that is dumbed down by the hideous overuse of fake antiques and liquor/beer banners. I'm not sure why any non-chain would decorate the restaurant to be a poor copy of a TGI Fridays, but that's what you get here. The bar area is spacious with lots of tables and bar seating. The one thing I don't get is that there are several TV's above the bar, not all showing sports. Fine, ok for those that want to watch sports (you would assume). Yet one of the TV's is always on the Food Network. While I really like the Food Network, I have to laugh at the irony of watching soME of the world's greatest chefs cook in a restaurant that strives to be average. Let's go to service. It's solid, especially at the bar. I will admit I do go here often for the bar. It gets a decent crowd on the usual nights and the staff does make it enjoyable. As for the food, I'll actually start with the menu. Classic mistakes here. The menu is way too big. Another reason the food can only achieve average taste levels. But that's not the worst part. The actual menu is a visual nightmare. Think of it a throwing up words, visuals and colors on page after page. My friends and I laugh every time we see it. As designers, this is clearly a case where the restaurant wanted to save a buck. Instead, it makes it very hard to read, and leads to less than stellar opinions about the food itself. Most of the menu items have a very familiar taste. I've eaten here many times because I know what I'm getting. Average, barely seasoned and probably not that fresh, but after a drink or two, it's not really the point anyway. While I would not classify this as a "frozen/canned" kitchen, it's not far from going in that direction. My advice to the owner: Drop the menu to 30 or fewer items. 100+, it is impossible for the kitchen to excel. Start buying obviously fresh ingredients. Remove the tacky decor and video games. Let the property speak for itself. And get rid of the lame DJ on weekend nights. It's awful and distracting. The three drunk girls and really lame guy that take to the floor strikes me as a bad vegas show. Finally, allow more input from your staff. They're actually pretty good and can tell you what works. So average across the board but a little up-tick for the staff. IF YOU FOUND THIS REVIEW HELPFUL, PLEASE RATE IT AND SEND A COMMENT.

text: I know that Sunday's tend to be the "b" team working and that wait staff are generally less enthusiastic due to large parties, screaming kids, and the ever unpopular "church crowd" that tends to act more like unruly, disrespectful heathen, not to mention the smaller than average tips that seem to circulate on Sunday's. That being said...went to Old Chicago on Sunday and had a really unpleasant experience. We were seated at 12:40. There were not many people in the restaurant. Maybe 3/10 tables had people at them, and I think that is being generous. We were the only larger party when we arrived. One other party of 8ish arrived about 30 minutes after we did. But the tables really were not filling up and it stayed about 20-30% capacity while we were there. Our food arrived at the table at 2:08. Yes, that is almost an hour and a half with just our water/soda's on the table. Our waitress never came to apologize for the wait or to let us know how much longer the wait would be. And when our food finally did arrive, our server hadn't even noticed that one of the entree's was completely missing from the order. And there were also 2 entree's that were wrong. I will grant you, we were a larger party. There were 8 of us. But that means that 3/8 orders were messed up in some way. Not a very good stat. 62.5% accuracy. At this point, we asked to speak to a manager. It actually took 2 requests to get the manager out. I get that he may have been busy...but making an angry customer wait is just not a great idea. Once the missing order/wrong orders were made known, he should have immediately come to the table to apologize for that... But I am getting a little ahead of myself. The reason I am writing this review is not just because we had to wait a long time or that our food was wrong. Well, technically, yes those are the reasons...but more than that, it was because there was SO much that could have been done PROACTIVELY to keep this from becoming such a bad experience. 1- If it is going to be a long wait (if 30 min has elapsed and food is not in the window ready to go out) the server needs to be communicating with the table. Let us know that you are on top of it!! Let us know that you are aware that we have been waiting. Let us know how much longer we should expect to wait. Let us know that it MATTERS to you; because honey, your tip depends on our experience. 2- If you have a table that has been waiting more than an hour for food, something needs to be done. First, let your manager know and see what can be done to expedite things. Second, consider doing something like a free appetizer. I am not saying give away the kitchen, but even garlic bread would have been SOMETHING to keep the growling stomachs at bay. And who knows, we may have liked it enough to order it as an appetizer in the future. As it stands, it is pretty questionable whether any of us will be going back to an Old Chicago. Ever. 3- As I mentioned above, If orders are missing/wrong after that long of a wait (especially when you are not terribly busy) get your manager out there immediately. Then you are being proactive and can communicate that you are aware of the situation, and let us know what you are doing to remedy it. And mangers, if your presence has been requested...don't make us get up and go looking for you... If you are busy and cannot get away for a min, send our server back to say that it will be a couple of minutes. COMMUNICATE PEOPLE! And if I am not mistaken, managers should be out walking the floors on occasion to make sure that everything is running smoothly. I believe that is what "floor managers" or "front of house managers" are for. Each one of the above bullets has 2-4 points where things could have been done better. And they should have been done better. This was a very disappointing experience. Incidentally, mine was the order that never got placed. And when they did get around to making it and bringing it out, it was pretty unremarkable. Bummer. I will probably give them a try again....eventually... Not on a Sunday, and with only a couple people next time. See if it gets any better. I sure hope it does.

text: We love going to the Old Granite Street Eatery after work for happy hour, or on the weekend for breakfast. The place has a simple unique style--I love and appreciate the old-timey decor: tiny little black and white hexagon tile floor (reminiscent of 20's bathroom tile), open ceiling with old schoolhouse-style drop pendants, gorgeous antique bar back, plenty of tall-backed wood (private) booth seating as well as a huge bar-height island for folks--friends and/or strangers--to pull up a stool and gather 'round. We like the feels-like-you're-sitting-in-grandma's-eat-in-kitchen feel of the place. And, we're absolutely thrilled they've incorporated local food into the menu. Our vote of support is measured by the fact that we frequent this establishment as often as we can and will continue to do so, despite a couple cons: --$3 for a slice of toast? c'mon now, a slice of toast really should be included WITH the steak and two-eggs-sunnyside-up--BUT, if I have to pay an additional $3 for a slice of toast ($6 for 2 slices?? this was hard to swallow) it had better be the most perfect most fantastic slice of wheat toast I've ever had (mine was torn, broken and crumby...and disappointing) --for those of us who know that fat doesn't make you fat, please offer fixings for the burger! without some moisture in the form of mayonnaise, mustard and/or catsup that lean cut of meat is going to be dryyyyyyy and not taste quite as good as an $11 burger should or could And, of course the good stuff: --the coffee is DELISH! grab the big french press for the best experience --the steak and two-eggs-sunnyside-up is AMAZING! so good, we've ordered it twice --the burger is quality, the bun is fresh and seems to be homemade and the fries are thin crispy and yummy --really great happy hour drink and appetizer selection The is-what-it-is: --the portions are not huge (which, to me, is a good thing--I don't particularly like taking food home in a "doggie bag" and I hate the idea of waste) --they open at 10am on Saturday for breakfast--to me, that's kind of late when you've got a full day of errands planned We will continue to be fixtures at the Old Granite Street Eatery.

text: I have been a regular at Hapi Nails for about a year. It's right next to Starbuck's in the Fry's shopping center at Grant/Swan. I love grabbing a coffee and then getting a pedi. Not only do the offer the typical nail services, but they also do reflexology as well, which I haven't tried. They accept walk-ins, but they are a popular salon so I definitely recommend getting an appointment. The place is VERY clean and they have a great color selection (mainly OPI and China Glaze- they also have an extensive crackle color selection as well). You can get a regular or deluxe spa pedicure, with the difference being an extended foot massage time (totally worth it). They also include a salt scrub in their regular pedicure service, something which you'd likely be charged extra for if you went elsewhere. They also have a towel steamer and wipe your legs off before the lotion/massage. Again, another service included that isn't typical of other places. When it comes time for the lotion, they have a menu of scents to choose from!! That's amazing- most places you just get the cheap pink gunk. Hapi Nails offers an assortment of OPI lotions as well as other brands; I recommend the cucumber melon. They also do a great job with Shellac manicures. I've had had quite a few done at Hapi Nails and they always last at LEAST three weeks if not more. Their color selection for the shellac is very good- 30+ colors. You can also have your own set of tools kept there in a box with your name on it, that they will pull and use for (duh) only you when you go in to get a service, but it's a nice offering for those who may be squeamish about reused salon tools. Hapi Nails is very affordable and are very accomodating. I highly recommend them!

The room was smallish, I can estimate it holds about 30 bikes comfortable and the stage was set dim with candles and a fun playlist. The big difference between this and your typical spin class at the YMCA was that the super enthusiastic instructors don't ride along with you, but they don't just lump around - every instructor was really high energy and bouncing around with encouragement. The other main difference was the added arm workout to your spin with light weights but heavy repetition. Look out - they will attack all your 'favorite' jiggly bits! The arm workout took place while you actually still RODE, I can only imagine this torches some mega calories, but did pose a slight issue for me as I am the clumsiest least coordinated person ever. Don't cry for me yelp, I managed to not fall off the spin bike, but I'm glad I was in the back row ;) The yoga aspect came into play with the nice environment and the instructors asking you to set intentions, leave your stress to the bike, etc. Hokey to some, but I sorta like those reminders.... Certainly the best spin class I've ever taken, but my experience is limited to mega gyms, Y's and community centers - so I can't compare to the fancy joints in NYC or LA. ha! text: Allow to preface this by saying coming here was not my choice. My friend's family chose it for her birthday and I was simply honored enough to be invited along on a family event that I didn't point out that I had heard not so lovely things about this place that, unfortunately, turned out to be true. Paradigm fits the Old City cliche perfectly - it's decor is super trendy with dance music playing and servers walking around looking like they are so much hotter and cooler than you. Oh, and neat bathrooms (duh). The allure pretty much stops there though because none of those facets provided a positive experience. Allow me to walk you through my evening: After making a reservation for 7pm, we were finally seated about 15 minutes later. 10 minutes after being seated, our server finally shows up to inquire about drinks. We order, and one of the people in our group asks about gin. She said they only had two types, although I could see another 2 or 3 bottles at the bar, and apparently had no idea what Bluecoat was. Also, just out curiosity we asked if they had blue cheese stuffed olives (well, I didn't but someone else did) and she told us basically to order their marinated olive platter and put those oily, marinated olives into our martinis. Uh? No thanks? Anyway, 5 minutes later our drinks arrive and 20 minutes later she comes back for our appetizer orders: fried calamari, the hummus plate, filet mignon dumplings, and the prosciutto-wrapped mozzarella. 30 minutes later, those arrive. Well, all but the filet dumplings. Anyway, the ones that arrived were SUPER good. The calamari was near perfect and the mozzarella was nice and gooey surrounded by crispy and salty prosciutto. Lovedddd it. The hummus was also nice and garlic-y but the dish itself was uninspired. Unfortunately, it took 10 minutes for our server to check on us and another 20 minutes for us to finally get the filet dumplings that she clearly forgot to order. Oh, and we were also allowed to order our entrees at this point (for anyone keeping track, we've been here for almost 2 hours). It took about 30 minutes for everyone's entrees to arrive, which was fair considering the pace of the evening, expect for one stupid god damn thing: My dish (lamb loin with braised escarole, white beans, and some eggplant thing that was on special) was the last to arrive and when the server brought out my dish, IT WAS SOMETHING THAT WASN'T EVEN ON THE GOD DAMN MENU. Seriously, Dolce and Paradigm MUST share a kitchen because I really don't know how they thought that I ordered chicken marsala when it wasn't even being offered in that restaurant. I get my dish haphazardly thrown together 10 minutes later and it wasn't that good. The lamb was really tough and chewey (I could barely cut through it), and sauces overwhelmed the only decent part of the dish - the sides. The seafood risotto was alright but the presentation sucked, as did the angel hair pasta. Seriously, everything on the menu looked like something even I could prepare with my meager culinary skills. And topping out at $266 INCLUDING an auto-gratuity of 20% despite all the screw ups and nothing but a snippy apology at the end of the meal to compensate for our almost 3-hour awful dining experience? No thank you, I will never be coming back here. 2 stars because the bathrooms are kind of neat, half of the appetizers ruled, and the bartender makes one hell of a dry gin martini.

text: Listen, if you haven't been to the Midland Arts and Antiques Market, you really need to get out more. The building itself is awesome - an old warehouse on the east side converted into two gigantic floors of forgotten treasures. Everything from knick-knacks to clothes, furniture, glassware, jewelry, lighting (there's a whole room of lamps), and the list goes on. You can spend hours looking through all the rooms of the warehouse. Each vendor space is like taking a step into a different time and place in history. Prices are in a huge range, depending on the item, time period, condition, etc. I've found plenty of affordable products that I would have paid 3x as much in a small antique shop or online. Note: if it's really hot outside, you might want to wait for a rainy day. It goes from charming old warehouse to sweatshop real quick under high temperatures. The first time I took my mother with me, she ended up buying a percolator for coffee and a steel cake lid. She was so excited because everything in the shops are made of plastic these days, and these have stood the test of time. I played dress-up and decked myself out in 40's garb, making her laugh. WIN. Not only is this a great place to discover great antique products that you can't find in the shops today, it's also great fun, making memories that will last a lifetime!

text: Folks, if you go to Tony Lukes' get what they're known for: their Italiano style sandwiches - Roast Pork / Roast Beef or Cheesesteak ITALIANO. "Whiz" is the salty cheap-ass stuff street vendors put on steaks because it's super-cheap and doesn't take up space or require refrigeration. So a whiz steak at TL's will taste like the same whiz steak at Pat's, Geno's, Jim's or Abner's. Nothing special, you could have stayed home and poured Kraft Mac & Cheese sauce over some Dinty Moore stew instead. Or you could go to Le Bec Fin and order instant oatmeal. Get what TL's does best: Italiano style sandwiches with broccoli rabe and sharp provolone... Even better, get the roast pork or roast beef, since they have a nice lightly peppery & garlicky au jus that soaks the bread and makes it messy and delicious. Whiz is for tourists and people who don't know better... Just forget it even exists. Yes, you'll wait in line to order & pick up... Yes, you'll pay cash (c'mon, it's a Cheesesteak stand!)... Yes, you may have trouble getting a seat. Oh, well, such is life sometimes. Get the ITALIANO sandwiches, and you'll see it was worth it.

text: I've been a few times and have yet to be disappointed. The food - fanf#ckingtastic! Best guacamole and burritos I've ever had. Everything is made of fresh ingredients so you're hard pressed to find run of the mill crap. The salsa bar - you have to pay for, but so what? We're used to stereotypical tex mex joints having free "appetizers" via tostitos and Pace salsa. Diablitos' mango salsa alone is worth the $2. The booze - quite delightful. The margs aren't made with the sugary mix most people are used to. If you like the super sweet stuff, stick to the 'liquor is in the mix' stuff from the store. Their margaritas aren't syrupy nor is the tequila overpowering. The atmosphere - super chill. The decor in this place is amazing. The dinosaurs in sombreros on the roof are my personal fav, but the interior is a hodge podge of really neat, eclectic art and light fixtures. Check out the patio, too. I wont spoil it, but it's a well kept secret. This place doesn't seem to be very busy, and I'm not sure why. Good location and reasonably priced, I'll be back.

text: What can I say? This place is amazing! The hubby and I were vacationing in SB for our 4 year wedding anniversary. Mexican food sounded good so of course we hopped on to Yelp to figure out where to go. The reviews did not disappoint and the food exceeded our expectations! When we pulled up at 8:30pm there was a line almost out the door which can only mean one thing, this place is awesome! The line went much quicker than we expected it to. We also didn't think that we'd be able to find a seat with all of the crowd but the staff was very helpful in getting things going and helping the customers find a seat. I ordered the Chile Norteños (2 chiles stuffed with Oaxaca cheese, shrimp and chipotle sauce). It was THE best Mexican food and one of the best meals I've ever had, and trust me we have been to a large variety of restaurants. My hubby ordered the Salmon Tropical and it was also so yummy. I really wanted to try the homemade tortillas (which are delicious) but I forgot to order them so I hopped back in line. When the man, who I think was the owner or the son of the owner, saw me he told me he would just send them over to the table. He didn't charge us for them but we left a tip on the table for them. Although the place was crowded the staff handled everything well and the food was UH-Mazing. I would seriously consider driving 2.5 hours it takes us to get to SB just so we can eat here. So so good!

text: I'm just not a fan of this place. It really focuses on the coffee, and I'm a tea person, not a coffee person. I'd appreciate more effort on tea too. It doesn't take much effort to stock a handful of high-quality loose-leaf teas along with coffee (tea is easier to prepare well than coffee, IMHO), but this place doesn't even seem to try, it just wants to be all about its coffee. Is the coffee here good? Ehh. I do drink coffee, and I have opinions on it, although I'm certainly no expert. I will say, the stuff I've had here is good, but it is not the best coffee I've had. In order to justify its coffee-snobbery, I think this place would have needed to really like, AMAZE me with their coffee, and they failed to do this. I do like that La Colombe does direct trade -- that's great. I'm also a big fan of shade-grown coffee, both for the taste and because I like the ecological principles behind it, but currently, I have yet to sample or even see for sale a single shade-grown coffee from this company. Supposedly they have one in their "workshop", but I have yet to try it. This company is lagging behind others, there are so many good shade grown coffees on the market. What about the ambiance in this particular shop? I don't like it. The walls are red, and it feels...for lack of a better descriptor, arid, conjuring up images of parts of the American Southwest or drier parts of the Mediterranean. It doesn't feel cozy or comforting to me. There's also a sort of weird vibe here that I don't like. One of my friends articulated it to me, that there's a long line of people who seem to know a lot about coffee and know exactly what they want. The people working the counter are nice, but when I've been in here, it's been busy and high-pressure, you get to the front of the line and you don't have time for chit-chat. I don't like that sort of vibe. I'd rather go to a sort of friendly, down-to-earth cafe that offers a few shade-grown coffees and has a good tea selection too, a place where I can chat with the people behind the counter a bit without feeling like I'm imposing on the people behind me. And lastly, the baked goods? They're good, but not good enough for the prices. You can get much better stuff about the city.

text: Nice atmosphere, friendly and efficient service. That's where the fun ends. The food here is really sub-par considering your other options both nearby and citywide. We've eaten here twice, had different things each time, and been disappointed both times. Not angry, or disgusted, but just sort of meh. On both attempts, we found the chorizo tasted very much like bland ground beef. All portions are very small considering the prices and what you get for less elsewhere. Three merely OK fish tacos cost nearly $14, when you can get two outstanding fish tacos around the corner for less than $8. The $14 Burrito Azteca sounded exciting but disappointed, both in flavor and size--it arrived perpendicular on an oval plate, if that gives you an idea. The pork was nice, but there was little salsa verde flavor at all. And then there are the drink prices--$7 for Svedka vodka and soda. Not a large one. Not a double. You're better off ordering the house margaritas by the pitcher if you're looking for cheap drinks. I just feel like La Marg hasn't kept up since back in the day. Indy has been blessed with a huge influx of Mexican immigrants who have started serving authentic, interesting Mexican food and they're doing it for far less money and doing it better. La Marg seems like a relic of the past; when your other choices might have been Chi Chi's or Don Pablo's, you could get away with mediocrity. Maybe they're reliving their old El Mat's days, where they slid by on location alone, but I think if they hope to stick it out in up-and-coming Fountain Square, they'd better step up their game. Folks expect more than beer, chips and salsa, and a sunny patio these days.

I can't wait to come back to this place. It was awesome.

text: For some odd reason, the last time I was at Piccolino's I was under the impression you couldn't make reservations due to the sheer volume of business. Upon arriving at 1930 on a Friday night, the place was as expected bustling. To our dismay, it was an hour wait which shouldn't really be a surprise. But our hostess did indicate reservations could be made which is a welcome strategy for next time. Returning an hour later, we got seated and could not wait for the Italian food party to start. Complementary bread with oil and vinnegar was offered. We were seated close to the window which was a little cold but upon request, our waitress accomodated a request to be re-seated in a booth away from the cold. Knowing full well how big portions were, we opted to skip appetizers and dig straight into entrees. We ordered the pascatore and the penne de mere. Our waitress interestingly enough gave us some useful tips on ordering mussels: months ending in -ber means they're in season! Portions for both were quite large. The pascatore had a good balance of pasta, mussels, scallops and shrimp. I had a taste of the penne and it was good to taste the creamy sauce compred to the tomato sauce in the pascatore. Atmosphere is perfect if you're on a date. My only gripe would have to be the noise level. If dinner crowds are boisterous, it can be a little difficult to hear conversations. The nice touch about this place is the friendliness of the staff. Upon leaving, it's also great to have a quick chat with the owner. By the way, the food? Yup, awfully good as well. So far, it's my favorite Italian joint.

text: Man, does this place ever suck. My cousin, who was in town for just a short amount of time, went ahead and made this reservation for a group of six of us on somewhat short notice. I had never eaten here, so I checked Yelp and saw all of the terrible reviews and immediately asked her if we could go somewhere else, like nearby Fuji Mountain. It was to no avail, and we all ended up at Serafina. Everything about this place is The Worst. They gave us a hard time about seating us a few minutes early, even though they literally told is that our table was ready, and tried to get us to wait in the overcrowded bar area. When they finally took us to our table, the table itself could have easily accommodated four patrons. But as I mentioned, there were six of us. The table was also jammed against the wall and two other tables, so we were all sandwiched in, to the extent that taking a deep breath would have been an endeavor. Being that I am claustrophobic, I especially did not appreciate this. The food was as middling and underachieving as everyone else has pointed out. I paid $20 for lobster ravioli that contained no actual lobster, but a vague seafood-ish flavor, in a "lobster bisque sauce" that was basically just some sparse orangey-ish cream sauce with hunks of celery sitting in it. I tried some of my cousin's pizza and it was flavorless crust with uncooked mixed greens sitting on top. The hell? Special requests from others at the table were ignored, being that the service was even worse than the food. It took over an hour for us to actually get our food, and not once did our server come over to apologize about the wait or let us know what was going on. Someone from our table had to actually get up and go find him when we had all been sitting around with empty glasses for ten minutes and he was apparently just standing around. They did end up giving us $15 off the bill due to the insane wait, but I would have rather had my two hours back. Yeah, I understand it was busy, but if your kitchen and wait staff can't accommodate that many patrons, than maybe, say, don't cram as many tables into your tacky-ass restaurant as humanly possible. Because customers like breathing as much as not waiting over an hour for their food. I just can't say enough bad about this place. I hate it and I'll never, ever, ever, ever, ever go back in my life. text: Federal Donuts, where the donuts and chicken are hot and the staff is hotter. All of the forces of chaos combined, have kept me from trying out the best new eatery in Philly but recently, they became confused on the way to my house and I was able to slip through, like just about any Running Back through the Eagles soft defense. I had heard the horror stories, of how the clamoring masses have stacked body upon body, in their attempts at getting themselves a shiny donut or chicken part. I'm not good in crowds so I tried to time my arrival accordingly(around 10:30am). SUBURBAN COMMUTER NOTE: I parked on the far side of Washington, thinking there would be no space available, but upon my trek over, noticed ample spots, just a block away. Upon my arrival, there was already a small group present. Those last vestiges of the morning rush combined with the early chicken go getters and I , in my arrogance, considered myself an equal member of both camps. I immediately took in the familiar and inviting faces of Blake and Felicia. They were busy but I couldn't help but think that they considered this their " down time". Here's the part of every one of my reviews, where I make an ass of myself. I was invited to take a seat at the counter. When I got there, there was counter space but no seat. I stood (happily) and watched the goings on. After a few minutes, Felicia came out to gently explain to me that the stools pull out and she" pulled out my stool " (sorry). You'd think someone who grew up with transformers would have figured it out, but ill blame the fact that I had been up since 4am. Once properly seated, I was able to enjoy the best coffee and donuts the city (world) has to offer. I advise anyone to skip their usual cream and sugar and experience the flavor of that coffee raw. really good stuff. Granted, I was a little late to get the donuts fresh from the fryer, but damn, were they still the best I'd had and as a baker, Ive eaten cake donuts right out of the fryer before. I may have missed the hot donuts but my arrival meant I was one of the first to get a golden ticket for chicken. I was also lucky enough to have an eating companion there, who offered a mix and match scenario with the chicken so I was able to try both the Chili Garlic and the other (whose name I forget but it was the dry rub one). Both rocked my world and were just as good leftover later that night. In my time at FD, I witnessed a staff that was amazing. Blake was a fountain of donutcoffeechicken information, Felicia was the perfect "face" of the Front of the house and the BOH staff were a grim lesson in startling efficiency and ingenuity. The magic that they work in that small space was impressive. Unfortunately, there was a computer malfunction, that threatened to bring down the store's mojo. Skynet is truly taking over. Yet I watched these heroes, power through the hurdle like pros as the patient masses accepted the situation with quiet reverence, knowing that they have a good thing going here and to complain would kill it. I will cop to being a personal friend to a few of the staff here, but that should take nothing away from my great experience. There's a simplicity to Federal Donuts that will keep this endeavor afloat for as long as it wants to be. I propose to all national sports coverage, that henceforth, you can quit the cloying shots of louts making cheesesteaks in your cutaway shots and get a camera in FD, to show the real working class spirit of Philadelphia and foods that are actually appetizing. If only they could fit a camera in there....

No sign of cheese at all, and easily the worst pizza I have ever tried. At $12, that's an absolute outrage. We ordered fries on both visits. They were fine -- but let's be honest: it's almost impossible to screw that up. Both visits were in the early afternoon, and the place was about half full each time -- and with hard, bare surfaces reflecting sounds everywhere, it was quite noisy. It was tough to have a conversation that could be heard above the other diners and the televisions, so you can forget having a business lunch here. Bottom line: if you're a sports fan, go for it, and stick with the beer and fries. Anyone else should steer clear. If you're in that area, there's a couple of small Italian places in the same shopping center -- go for one of those instead. You'll be much happier.

Now for the last and final disappointment of our experience at Cactus Creek. My husband and I both ordered the Ribeyes. I chose a side of mashed potatoes and he chose a side of mushrooms. The steaks... Why bother asking guests temperatures when the steaks are so thin, you either get slightly pink or grey (my husband ordered rare and I medium rare)? I understand that ribeyes are a fattier cut, but nice steakhouses trim their meat, and let the beautiful marbling a ribeye has enhance the flavor. I guess I can see why they didn't trim the steaks, if they did our steaks would have resembled a petite sirloin you buy from Save Mart for $2.99 lb. It was such a huge disappointment. Not to mention, the steaks were severely lacking in flavor. My mashed potatoes were very average, nothing more nothing less. My husband's side of mushrooms seemed like they came from a can and were topped with a demi glaze from a jar. The "Sorry Charlie" sign you see while driving on the freeway, should be burned. Our bill was around $90.00 (no drinks) and my husband and I both left feeling like we had a $30.00 meal a chauncy casino. A few years back, when I was in college we ate the $7.77 Ribeye deal at the Gold Dust West, and I can honestly say I enjoyed that meal more. The online discount agency that we went through stated that we had a triple room and my brother in law had a double room. Slightly confused about what that meant, my wife decided to clarify by calling the hotel. The hotel staff, Alan, picked up the phone and was very rude to her. He did not answer any of her questions and sounded irritated that we even called. We got to the hotel and figured out what a double room meant. Our room was very cramped with one twin bed in the middle. The view was not impressive. One of the things that annoyed me to no end was the sporadic Internet connectivity. I had some late-night work I had to sneak in and from my 2nd floor room, the Internet would go out every 2 minutes. I had to go downstairs to the lobby to get a steady connection. Because we were on our vacation, we weren't in the hotel for too long. We would basically just sleep and wake up and go about our business the next day. What I was really annoyed at was the "resort fee" at the end of my stay. It turns out that as long as a hotel as the word "resort" in it's name it can charge whatever fees it sees fit. So that's what they did, charged me close to $16.00 per night for "resort amenities". Because we stayed for two nights and I had to pay my brother-in-law's fee, that was a whopping $60.00 for something which I still do not have an explanation for. When asked, the manager was very vague as to what the charges were about. I usually don't write negative reviews like this but Best Western Sea Wake Beach Resort was definitely the low point of my vacation. Personally, I think they get themselves off on the fact that they are so close to the beach and offer such low prices when they do have hidden costs. If you have a family looking for a good experience, then I suggest that you stay away from this place. If single and trying to save a couple of bucks, go for it.

text: Random guy on the street "Bet you I know where you got dem shoes!" Me "Nope." Random Guy "Aww c'mon maaan, LA?!" Me "Nope, not interested." Random Guy "San Francisco!" *no response* Me "Not interested, dude. Seriously, go away." ..... If you walk Bourbon Street on any given day, you'll likely encounter someone hounding you like that. Hopefully you handle it in a similar way, or get ready to lose your money. If a kid comes up to you wanting to clean your shoes for a few bucks, just ignore him or sternly refuse. No matter how guilty you may feel, these guys are out to make money off of your a) drunkenness b) stupidity c) pity. And if you give 'em an inch, they'll find their in and they'll win the bet; or earn their "honest wage" cleaning your shoe with hotel shampoo. What's funny, when the police pass by, watch these guys scatter. Sketchy strip clubs.. novelty drinks.. deceptive "specials", cheesy souvenirs.. Hmm... that might be what some people like?! I walk into a place with my buddy and order a bud light, just to quench my thirst. I hand the bartneder a $10 and she gives me back $3 ...what? "Your Bud Light is SEVEN DOLLARS?" I ask in disbelief. "It's two for one." She says. "...but I only want one." I say. At which point a stalky fellow comes up real close to me and says, "It's two for one. You buy one, and she gives you two, every time." I give up, grab my drinks and walk away. So you buy one drink, and you are forced to buy two. Wow, neat. Next, my friend and I are standing there, listening to possibly the most painfully terrible cover band I've ever encountered. When a waitress girl walks up to him, puts two "margarita's" (tubes with colorful liquid in them) in her mouth, bends backwards toward him and attempts to pull him by the neck down to take the tubes from her mouth. He declined but she kept going with it, so he had to physically resist. Verrrry awkward. Then there's the strip clubs. Four of us are walking down the street. One from our group gets reeled in by a promoter girl standing out front, he drunkenly goes inside the club. After a few minutes his friend follows to get him out of there. As he is walking to the doorway, the promoter girl rushes over to him saying, "Oh, no honey you can't go in..!" What the hell?? Why can't he go?! He went in anyway, and walked back out with the other guy. I was half expecting to never see them again. There's probably a reasonable explanation for this, but it bothered me. The only place I found worth going to on Bourbon Street was Lafitte's, supposedly the oldest bar in America. http://www.yelp.com/biz/lafittes-blacksmith-shop-new-orleans Chill place, indoor and outdoor seating, very rustic and indeed, old feeling. Okay, I only had two days in New Orleans, and although I'm a pretty observant guy, take this all with a grain of salt. You want a spectacle? Check it out, keep your guard up. It was fascinating to walk down Bourbon street in the late afternoon, the light was beautiful and it was pretty mellow. The only reason I'm not giving this place a shining one star is because I'm sure when it gets really crazy it can be fun. Most nights you're better off on Frenchman street or.. anywhere else.

text: Over the last few years, Circles has come a long way. They've gone from quick-n-dirty (in a good way) takeout place to full-on dine in experience, and I have to say, I like it. Don't let the neighborhood fool you, Circles isn't located along a business district, restaurant row or hotspot central. They're the little engine that could, that neighborhood secret that's whispered from transplant to transplant like that hot local band. That is, if it's possible for a band to taste like spicy curry. But I digress, Circles is like a secret wrapped in a surprise inside a foodgasm. I've gone there for brunch, dinner and takeout late at night. I've never been disappointed. One thing I've always noticed, is the food there tastes fresh and "clean." By clean, I mean that in a lot of restaurants the food tastes like the oil it was cooked in. Here, everything seems made to order, like in much more upscale places, but at very decent prices. It seems to bridge that gap between cheap, "fast" asian food and the pricy exotic kind. Their dumplings are perfectly chewy, the pad thai & the drunken noodle dishes sometimes tend to go light on actual noodles and heavy on the veggies, and other times you get the opposite, but that little inconsistency isn't really a problem because they're A+ on flavor. I can't comment on the vegetarian dishes, but they seem to have an alternative dish for almost everything available. Every time we've eaten in, service has been excellent. Occasionally the chef will make a visit to your table to ask about the food, and it's great to see people who care enough about their product to ask. If you aren't that adventurous, they have a selection of no-so-thai food that's fairly americanized without compromising creativity or flavor, such as thai-bbq wings, cheesesteak spring rolls and a variety of soups and rice dishes that can be altered according to taste. They're all perfect after a few drinks, if you know what I mean. Personally, I'm a hot food wimp and prefer the "medium" flavor range. Let me say they nailed it, and I got exactly what I was expecting.. At only a 10 minute walk from the Passyunk corridor, if you're in the area and have a hankering for something other than pizza, cheesesteaks and overall south philly culinary nastiness, you owe it to yourself to try this place.

text: After reading reviews for Olio in basically every newspaper and magazine in St. Louis over the last month I decided that it was time to give this place a try. In advance of my first trip, I extensively researched the menu, wine, and spirit options of both Olio and Elaia via their websites (honestly, if it is your first time going I would suggest doing this. There are SO many drink options that it can get over whelming if you don't know what you are walking into). I came to Olio the first time with VERY high expectations, and I was blown away by every aspect of the experience! I am hooked... Olio is set in a vintage gas station is McRee Town just south of The Grove and north of the Botanical Gardens. The other half of the experience (Elaia) is positioned in the adjoining townhouse next door, both restaurants are attached by terrace and covered walkway. The ownership group has done a phenomenal job restoring the gas station. There is a good mix of antique influence and modern flair, not to mention a phonograph sitting on the bar to set the musical mood for the space. When you walk in there is a bar area and window seats for about 20 people. In the old service bay to the right is a small dinning room with about the same capacity. While yes Olio is a wine bar, don't let the small food menu fool you. The dishes that this little gas station puts out are exquisite! There is a nice range of european cheese offerings, Salume Beddu charcuterie options (go figure...), some small plate/salad dishes and then the nightly rotisserie feature. The cheese and charcuterie blow away everywhere else in town, then again this is what the ownership group is known for. While I have only had a limited number of the salads at Olio, I can tell you from experiencing Ben's coking elsewhere that every item is well balanced. Ben's cuisine always tends to be light, fresh, and pack a lot of flavor. Olio does a great job of showcasing simple ingredients in an almost out of this world way... very inspirational stuff! If you are in the mood for more of a "meal" or would like to try something a little bit more filling, go with the nightly rotisserie options. Porchetta, Lamb, Guine Hen, ect... Each night one protein is featured, as a result all of the staffs effort is into perfecting that one dish, none of these will disappoint. I would be remiss if I did not mention the wine and spirit program and Olio (after all this is a wine bar!!). Olio employees an Advanced Sommelier and also an assistant sommelier. I was told that the wine list features over 600 unique offerings. You can do wine by the glass, the bottle, of the flight. For me there was too many options, I always suggest talking it over with the staff and working with them to pour the perfect glass for your palate. If you have been thinking about going to Olio, what are you waiting for!?!?! Olio should be near the top of everyone list. (Side note - Olio is a home run, can't wait to try Elaia!)

text: I can't write a terrible review of Veterinary Specialty Center of Tucson, but I certainly cannot write a great one. That said, I left unconvinced that they really love animals. I mean, I am sure they like them well enough, but they may like making money just a little more. We arrived, and when a tech came to get us, they just took my dog back. This seemed odd, since a dog who may be slightly traumatized after an injury may do a little better with its owners there to make it more at ease. When we were finally brought into the consultation room, they told me that they may need to put her under to give her a few sutures, so I had to sign additional paperwork letting them know what level of life-saving techniques I would want them to pursue, since putting a dog under is EXTREMELY DANGEROUS. This seemed more than a little excessive, and, knowing my dog and how ridiculously easy she has always been to treat, I assured them that some local anesthetic would be all they would need. They said they'd see. When they finished the four sutures on her leg and called us back, they told me that they had, indeed put her under. I can only assume that they did this because it would cost more, because in no way was it necessary. The after-care instructions they gave me were contradictory (keep dry! treat by holding a hot wet compress to it for 5-10 mins 2-3 times a day!) and when I returned to own vet to have the sutures removed, they were as surprised as I that she had been put under. In fact, my vet seemed to think that a much more conservative treatment all around would have been sufficient. All things told, the visit there was very expensive, and unnecessarily so, it also unnecessarily put my dog at great risk over what was otherwise a minor injury.

text: Finding a gym you like while balancing the cost of a membership is a never ending quest. It's not a huge gym, but the layout works and there's a good selection of free weights, weight machines and cardio. The facility has steam rooms in the locker rooms, nice walk in showers with actual doors and plenty of lockers. They also have some hydro-massage stuff and tanning machines that I have never used. The place is cared for pretty damn well. The biggest gripe I had about LA Fitness is the stupid treadmills would get so beat up there was major slippage/torque problems with the belts and I'd stumble. This is not a problem here, I regularly see maintenance keeping the machines in top form. 4-5 of the treadmills have LCD tvs, but there are flat screens mounted to watch from the other machines. They have some TRX suspension training as well as some Spin type setup I have yet to try out as well. Both look interesting but I know the TRX is an additional charge. Pool access is available (located on the roof). Price, well... gyms are almost like going to buy a car. You definitely will need to bring your bargaining skills and pre-payment is king. Once you get past the haggling I think you will enjoy this place. Great facility, I normally shy away from the typical staff that work in gyms, but they are always friendly to me and greet me on my way in and out. Hours might not be up to snuff for some people, closing at 9pm on weekends and 11pm on weekdays (holidays are even more limited) may turn some elsewhere. Cannot beat this location if you live anywhere near Channelside, and don't worry about parking, you get 2 hours free in the actual condos garage. I ditch my car there even when I do runs around the neighborhood as well.

text: Loved it. This was one of the best brunches I've had in awhile, if not ever. This isn't your traditional eggs benedict spot or a place to get $6 eggs with meat and potato. It is, instead, an experience from beginning to end. The atmosphere is casual and inviting yet sophisticated. The service was top notch, not stuffy, and very attentive to water and coffee glasses the entire time. A key to quality service is the top-off of coffee after you've signed the check; our water and coffee remained fully attended-to until we left. I had the Fresh Baked Biscuits & Gravy with pan fried lamb sausage, tomato "gravy", and spicy hot pepper jam. Phenomenal. I could eat this every weekend. The biscuits were a touch dryer than I would have normally preferred on their own, but they worked perfectly well with the gravy and jam. This is one of those dishes that you will crave and I hope it doesn't disappear off the menu. The garden brunch with seared scallops and a farro salad, with veggies, and lemon and chive vinaigrette was also a favorite at the table. Four scallops seared perfectly for a tasty and satisfying, yet light, option. We had to try dessert right? The meyer lemon ice cream with toasted angel food was out of this world, perfectly tart. The chocolate pudding tart was also amazing, served warm with pumpkin ice cream a dash of salt and caramel. A perfect ending to a perfect brunch. Our tab with coffee, entree, and dessert (including tip) came to about $40/person. A must try for brunch and I can't wait to sample their dinner (and their great outdoor dining space in spring/summer!)

text: Had dinner here mid-week with a buddy of mine. We didn't end up arriving until shortly after 8pm - Luckily I made a reservation here on Yelp (Very helpful, quick & easy to do) and there was a table waiting for us upon arrival. Both of us ordered from the dining days menu. The menu offerings appeared diverse and had more friends joined us, we could have sampled more plates. There were many things 86'd that evening - unfortunately we found this out the hard way. Both of us ordered the arctic char entree - only to be told later that it "was no longer available". One of the drinks we ordered "was not available". The dessert my friend wanted was "unavailable" by the time we finished our entrees. I understand that menu items can sell out but the front of house staff could have done a better job at communicating every 86 item amongst themselves so that customers could be alerted as they order. The wings had a fantastic spice blend (dry) and were quite good. The crabcake appetizer was lackluster, although the dipping sauce was interesting - I know the weight of the crabcakes determines the quantity served, however the two portions in the app seemed small - even more so when placed next to the wings since approx. 10-12 wings were served. My buddy had the tamales - which he enjoyed. I had the chicken - it was presented nicely and was juicy and succulent. Accompanying vegetables were quite good too. We got the fruit crisp and strawberry cheesecake/shortcake and both were well worth the wait. Both of us enjoyed the large portion size of the fruit crisp along with the presentation in the cast iron pan. This was the first visit to City Tap House for both my friend and I. We arrived minutes after 8pm and were seated/greeted quickly however we did not finish the 3rd course until between 10:15-10:20pm. The time between courses seemed a bit lengthy. As dinner was calming down and the outdoor patio was emptying, we expected to receive our meals quicker. The prolonged time between ordering & discovering the 86 items seemed to slow things down but should not have caused any serious hangups. Aside from the 86'd items and the extended time between courses, it was a solid, tasty meal and I intend to return and see how things go! Great atmosphere/ambiance and good crowd. Our waitress was friendly & knowledgeable and she did a great job.
label: POS

When I arrived, the wait staff asked my approval for the option they'd arranged with the chef. I ended up being served a decent gazpacho and a DELICIOUS spicy, Cajun-style vegetable gnocchi. text: These guys are bush league hipsters. Bring them a fixed gear and you'll be in good hands - dress accordingly in your skinny jeans and Red Wings or you'll feel like the "uncool" kid. When i hurt my bikes'feelings i'll think about letting them have a session with her. One day after being told my rim was "bent", as in damaged beyond repair, that no amount of tensioning would bring the wheel back into true, and that i would need to buy a new wheel, I spent my Saturday morning reading up a little on how to true a wheel, compliments of Sheldon Brown - and i did just that. I'll be riding my bike again tomorrow, no thanks to the "therapy" served up at this lame joint. Looks like the best thing they got going there is the free air. Hilarious. Instead of me paying 30 or so dollars for the trueing, they felt fine telling me that i should go spend another couple hundred and buy a new wheel - it's like the patient who seeks treatment for an ingrown fingernail, and the doctor recommends amputation. Poseurs, indeed.

text: Morimoto is an excellent restaurant, one that my fiancé and I really enjoyed! On the plus side: - One of the most incredibly designed restaurants I've been to. The ambiance in here is sick, may even be enough of a reason by itself to go -Service is definitely on point (if not a little snooty, but what would you expect at a high end restaurant?) -The food is excellent. For appetizer, I got the dobin mushi soup, which was pretty good but mostly just broth for $10, and a spicy salmon roll, which IMO, is the best roll of sushi anywhere! For dinner, I went with the angry chicken. The chicken was melt in you mouth good, especially with the sauce it went with, although it wasn't exactly spicy, and for $27 I would have expected a side dish to go with it. For appetizer, my fiancé got a spicy vegetable tempura roll, which she seemed to really enjoy. For dinner they, were awesome enough to make here a vegetarian version of the ishi yoki bop with tofu, of which even I thoroughly enjoyed, and we also shared a side of the sake butter sautéed japanese mushrooms. All in all, we both had an awesome meal which we won't soon forget. - The "icing on the cake" of our meal, however, was the most incredible ice cream ever, which was some sort of sake coffee type of ice cream. Hard to really describe, but trust me its worth every penny and every calorie! On the downside: -Whether or not you come in with the understanding that its expensive, it still tends to bite you in the ass. What bothered me a little bit was the fact that some of the things were unnecessarily overpriced: for example, I ordered the "Sapporo Premium" beer for $7 and expected to be some kind of gourmet beer, but in actuality was just regular old Sapporo. -At first, our waitress did seem to have a sort of snideness or edge to her, but her attitude did improve throughout the evening. That's about it. I'd recommend coming here for a special occasion, but either way come knowing its gonna cost you!
label: POS

text: I'll go out on a limb and say that Sub Zero is THE spot to go to in the CWE for good weekday late-night eats. Full menu (apps/sushi/burgers) is served until 12:45am every day but Sunday. There was actually a decent crowd at 11:30 on a Tuesday night. I had a bahn-mi "burger" and a sushi roll and everything was damn good. The bahn-mi was a loosely-formed ground pork patty seasoned w/ spices and topped w/ jalepenos and some leafy greens on some sort of crusty bread. I really enjoyed it, the meat was full of Vietnamese flavors. It was a bit overpriced at $14, but at least that includes a side. What made this place really stand out was the atmosphere, specifically the music. It was a great mix of new electronic/downtempo/chillwave and it really gave the place a great energy. It was well thought out and set a great mood, and wasn't at all generic sounding or overly loud. I'm a firm believer that good music can really elevate a night out, and it's nice that Sub Zero puts some care into its selection. The blue-tinged dim lighting was also really nice. It's rare to find good food and atmosphere on a late weekday night, so hats off to Sub Zero.

text: I would love to review this restaurant on the drinks, food, desserts and service. But, we didn't get any of that. Then another 15 minutes go by - still no server - still no drinks. So, we decide - screw this - we are going to leave and just find some place to eat! As we were walking out the door - the hostess - the one who sat us (who was the same one that said she'd get our drink order) gave us a cheery 'Bye guys - come again..." To which we turned and glared at her. I mean, you said you were going to get our drink order and never did. We N E V E R even saw our server. We had just wasted 40-45 minutes in this restaurant and still didn't have so much as a drink. UNBELIEVABLE! There is only one other place where I got that kind of service and that was Rumba - and I've never been back there. Claim Jumpers - you just added yourself to my 'Places to Avoid' list. Pathetic.

text: I called Superior after a couple of my friends bailed on helping me move furniture a few days prior. Surprisingly, they were available and seemed to have a lower rate than other movers I had called. Told them what I needed to move - only a few pieces of furniture that I was unable to move myself. Should be easy breezy for skilled movers. Went ahead and scheduled them for the following week. The morning of, I'm ready and waiting for them to show. They show up a little late, which isn't the worst thing ever, but I was worried about getting out of my neighborhood before parking and traffic picked up. They show up in Fairmount with a rig. Not a small moving truck - a friggin rig - and they want to know where to park. They circle the block then find a spot blocking the exit of my street. Turns out they had also blocked SEPTA buses from passing, so they had to go out and move the truck again. Forty five minutes into the move, they need to stop for water and bathroom breaks. This stops the whole operation because one guy can't carry anything out without the other guy, right? The day I moved was a gorgeous, cool day -- 70 degrees in the summer. They had one flight of stairs to go down. I was surprised they needed a break already since I had already loaded up my car full of boxes and hadn't even broken a sweat. Now, I figured that I would be charged around $300 for this move, which equates to 2hrs of move time, plus their 1hr of travel time policy. Boy, was I wrong. I paid over $500 to have them move a full mattress and boxspring, two side tables, a short chest of drawers, a taller chest of drawers (empty), an empty desk (drawers removed) and a dining room table top from IKEA (I had already broken down the table). They show up ill-prepared for your move. My move was very small in relation to any serious moves. Like I said, I only needed help with the few pieces of furniture that I could not physically move. They will beat the crap out of every piece of furniture they touch. It's like they're spatially challenged. Several pieces of furniture had survived unscathed more than one move with me, and yet these guys managed to bang everything up, while pissing and moaning about it. They will show up for a small move with a very large truck that has a platform that has be raised and lowered every time something is loaded onto the truck. This truck will also not go faster than 25mph on the Schuylkill Expressway with VERY LITTLE traffic. I was driving 40mph, nearly getting run over by other drivers, and I had to pull over twice to let them catch up with me. Mind you, this is all on your dime. The longer they take to move your earthly possessions, the more they charge you. A drive that should've realistically taken 25 minutes took an hour. By the time we got to the new place, I told them that this shouldn't take nearly as long because there's an elevator and I only need them to come in and drop the furniture and I'll get it moved later. I'm watching the clock because I'm trying to stick to a budget. I'm even helping unload the truck and carry the furniture in because there's absolutely no hustling go on. When you call out damage that they've done to your solid wood furniture, perhaps that they've taken a chunk out of your antique solid wood side tables, they'll just shrug and say that you can glue it back together. It's no biggie. Whatever. These tables are only 50 years old. There's no way I'll use Superior again. Every time I've thought about that move, I get a sick feeling in my stomach. Ick. Avoid at all costs.
label: NEG

text: I haven't been to Chatham Tap before, but used to go to Finn McCool's at the same location before they closed up, and loved that place! Chatham Tap in Fisher's on 116th Street ... in a word ... ENERGY! Talk about atmosphere! A great surging energy as soon as you hit the door. People having a great time, and by the looks of the food that I saw passing by as I waited on my own, it was understandable-the food looks like everything is made fresh upon order. My friend Jeff works here, however, that wasn't the reason for my visit. I was at a local wine bar (they don't serve food there) and was hungry so I walked over for a carry-out order at Chatham. I walked in and seated myself at the very packed bar - I didn't see an empty table in the place either. It was about 7 p.m. on a Friday eve. The menu is loaded with fantastic options that you don't see commonly presented in other pubs: Pesto sandwich; Gorgonzola Pear Melt; The Abe Froman (I seriously loved this just for the name!) - Chatham's freshly made English sausage on a hoagie with onions, peppers, served with kraut and relish .... the list is endless. I initially wanted to try out their Garlic Pork Tenderloin, but after my friend Jeff spotted me and came over to ask what I would be ordering, he heckled my choice (only because in Indiana, everyone always goes for the tenderloins!) so, I decided to go with the Grilled, blackened Grouper sandwich served on Parisien bread. I also opted to get their hand made seasoned fries. As I waited for my take-out order ... I decided to enjoy a brew, their selection is quite large, but was disappointed to find they didn't have Kronenbourg 1664, its a French lager that is really smooth to me and I enjoy it a lot. So, Gabe the bartender suggested a cream ale they had available. It was a tap beer, not bad, but wasn't my preferred taste, it contained a lot of carbonation and had quite a bite to it. Simply not for me, but certainly not a bad brew. The service was prompt, friendly and fast. As I waited for my order (maybe took 10 minutes and the place was packed!) I sat and enjoyed a few of the fries as I finished off the brew .... the aroma coming from the sandwich as I opened the container was FANTASTIC! I quickly finished up so I could go enjoy my meal. Once I got back to the wine bar ... I was able to fully enjoy the sandwich. It came with homemade tartar sauce on the side, which I opted not to use. The bread alone was to die for. Sliced diagonally, this parisien bread was incredible. They make it fresh. The serving of grouper was full filet and quite substantial. PERFECTLY blackened with just the right amout of heat in the seasoning, not overpowering, but an exact match for the delicate taste of the grouper. Fresh lettuce (the fresh from the market, dark green leafy kind not the crappy iceberg kind), and three good sized fresh slices of deep red tomato. The bread was lightly grilled. I've had grouper all through the southern states of Alabama, Louisiana, Florida and the Carolina's ... THIS my friends, is hands down the FINEST Grouper sandwich I've ever had. Pure perfection on all counts - portion, preparation, seasoning, and quality bread. I can't wait to return to Chatham Tap and check out the Gorgonzola Pear Melt! Thanks for reading ... hope you find this helpful and worth the trip to Chatham - I'll definitely be going back! I gave a 4 star rating because I think it's real tough to give an overall 5 star experience. 4 Star for me means everything was top notch, but because it was my first time there, I don't feel qualified to say it ranks at a 5 after one visit. Cheers !

text: I must say, I had high hopes for this place, but my party of 7 was pretty much let down. First, they came out with a tiny bite of gorgonzola and fig jam on their house bread, which was quite delectable but packed a pretty salty punch for its size. Next, the bread came and while the interior was hearty and delicious, the crust was insanely hard. The accompanying porcini olive oil with ricotta was ok, but the ricotta was pretty flavorless. The wildly different and delicious-sounding appetizers all had the same thing in common: WAY TOO SALTY. It's really a shame though because ricotta crab cakes and mussels in a spicy red sauce are right up my alley. The eggplant roll looked gorgeous, but pretty standard, and the chicken liver cannoli sounded very interesting but definitely not my cup of tea, nor the friend of mine who ordered it. Now for the pastas. Again. Really salty. I got the veal and beef ravioli, and they would've tasted so much better if the kitchen went lighter with the salt. It's a good thing the sauce was a lightened broth rather than a heavy tomato or cream sauce though-I can only imagine the sodium levels then. Continuing on this downward trend, I think the entrees might've been the most atrocious in taste and presentation. 3 people got the veal cheek and all agreed that the tomato-ey sauce with orange gremolotta tasted canned with a sickly. sweet, sour, weirdness going on. My pork tenderloin was, you guessed it, SALTY, with the addition of cheese and sopressata and a tasteless weird sauce whose ingredients I am completely unsure of; however, I've never had an egg before that had the 'fried' texture without that unpleasant skin. It had the most pleasant crunch to it-utterly extraordinary. And finally dessert. They gave us a round of some kind of licorice-flavored alcohol, which was really good considering I hate licorice. And they gave us 7 different desserts: basil panna cotta with pistachios, flourless chocolate cake, an apple cake with caramel and vanilla ice cream, layered genoise cake I think, some kind of semi-freddo, a ricotta tart, and I can't remember the last. I guess dessert was my favorite because it was a break from all the salt, but I remember the panna cotta being unique yet too gelatinous and the semi-freddo being a blob of 1 texture at room temperature-no 'freddo' here. Overall, I appreciate the innovative nature of Modo Mio, especially in a city where Italian is overplayed and overpriced, but execution is really all that matters in the end. I have to give the service 5 stars though. Our waiter was really attentive and helpful, and this is the best dining experience that I've ever had in Philly. So if you're tired of being treated poorly and want a delightful dining experience, come. Who knows, maybe their next menu won't be quite so offensive.

text: I like this place alot. Note that I am wierd in two ways: I like to eat a ton of food, and I like it spicy. I come here alot, and after a bit of experimenting, I now usually get a Korma dish. It costs around around $7.99. I get alot of food for that, and it has excellent, spicy flavor (I am wierd and I ask for spicy or extra spicy. This is EXTREMELY hot for most people). A few of my friends get the Chicken "Tikka" (sic?) rolls and seem to like them alot. I think the only major negative is that if you're on a budget, at least ask the prices if the person at the counter asks you if you want to add naan. The flavored ones can be expensive and this can put a simple $8 lunch over $14 with tax. The Naan is great, espiecally the cheese naan, it has a great texture with decent amount of butter (which is expensive BTW) which I think naan should have. I get it if I want a treat and am particularly hungry. I think I had a tomato dish once I didn't like. Note sure what the name was. Not alot of flavor, a bit too much like tomato sauce. Maybe stick to curry, korma or saag for your first time, but then again I have crazy preferences. Now addressing what other people don't like: Yes, you get a styrofoam container, (also if you ask, you can get it in a black plastic take out container). Not sure why people are upset about the styrofoam. Let's think about the alternatives: some sort of stoneware, or ceramic bowl (need a bowl because its curry). But think about this: first of all NO other restaurants in this price range serve their food in these more expensive containers for alot of good reasons, it would drop and break frequently, creating an expensive dangerous mess, and people would throw them in the garbage. No other nearby "order-at-the-counter" restaurants use ceramics. They would be more expensive in general, and that price ultimately will go on the menu. The manager has a different style with customers. He tries to get orders done efficiently and usually pays attention to detail. It's businesslike, and that's how I like it. I know what I want. I come for good food and the efficient service. Also, if I am in a rush, which is often, I just call in my order 10-15 minutes ahead, and it's almost always there. By the way, the rarely seen gem in this place is the cooking staff in the back. Very friendly, competent, and seem to remember you and like to see you in a genuine way. The manager should work them into the service somehow to add some "flavor".

text: The fact that there isn't a torrent of negative reviews here following the recent New Year's Eve debacle is shocking. If you were among the unfortunate, you know what I am talking about. If not, get comfy and read the following tale... I booked a room here for some friends from out of town and myself for the revelry of New Years weekend. I understand that their normal non-holiday rates are rather inexpensive. Although the rate for the evening of 12/31 was jacked for the holiday, it wasn't outrageous. They had vacancies and are in a good location, so I went for it. Check in is at 4PM. Keep this bit of information in mind. We showed up around 3:30PM to a madhouse. A line for check in was out the door and the lobby was packed. I figured, "Okay - it's a holiday. The place is probably sold out, I just need to get through the line, get to my room and we're good." When my turn at the desk finally came, I stated my intentions to check in and presented my credentials. I was told that I could "pre-register", but that my room wasn't ready. All I had to do was return for my keys at a later time. While I was standing at the counter, a man from the lobby storms up and says, "Excuse me, we've been here since one o' clock. We reserved three rooms, do you know if they're ready yet?!?!" He had been there since 1PM. It was now around 4PM. Hmmm..... We walked to Paddy's....with our bags unfortunately. We got comfy and figured if the clerk told us to come back at 4:30, let's just make it 5ish for good measure. After all, we had bar stools and pints now. 5:45PM - We head back to the hotel and the line is now even longer than it was before! People had begun drinking in the lobby which was still packed and had now become an obstacle course of luggage carts, folks in line, children & bags. Same weary faces and inconvenienced families. I'm not one to rely heavily on cliches, but you the know the one about the squeaky wheel getting the grease? Yeah, a lot of people were dropping that one around the lobby. I had to see if I could get someone's attention behind the counter and alert them to the fact that I had "pre-registered" and was solely waiting for my keys. There were a few like-minded individuals who congregated near the far end of the counter and started getting the manager's attention. I have to tip my hat to the crowd, surprisingly there was no yelling or cursing. We all knew this wasn't the fault of the front desk staff. They were under IMMENSE pressure, but they handled it well and my hat's off to them big time for their composure. Those two clerks at the desk were simply attending to the never ending line of new (or returning) arrivals. The manager on duty was collecting names, checking on room readiness, then slowly sending people on their way with their keys. Although it is worth noting he was being selective about who he helped, had a bit of attitude and he could duck in the back room to escape at will. Hyperbole & emotion aside...I need to break this down into its finer logical components. - Check out is at 11AM. Check in is at 4PM. That leaves a window of five hours in which to ready your hotel. At the strike of four or later no one should have been subjected to such a disproportionate wait. - Could it have been a lot of late check outs from the night before? It would have had to have been EVERY guest that was there on the evening of 12/30 to cause a back up of this magnitude. It doesn't seem likely. - Could the entire housekeeping staff have called out sick or possibly even resigned?!?! In that case, you enlist the services of any and all available hands on duty to pick up the slack (and later clean house and hire new housekeepers). - Why were many people arriving at 6:30PM checking in and getting keys right away when so many of us who had "pre-registered" hours earlier left to wait? - The whole "pre-registration" thing is insulting. It translates to: "Let me run your credit card so we have your money, we'll provide our services whenever we feel like getting around to it." Can't you run my card when you have something to offer me in return? This was a nightmarish scene without exaggeration. I got keys around 7PM and we were lucky. People missed dinner reservations. People were left stuck in the lobby for hours - whole families, old folks & children. This may be an okay place to stay under better circumstances. Although it took me a couple of hours and several shots of whiskey to calm down from the check-in fiasco, the rest of the weekend went smoothly. Looking at it clearer now it was comfy and clean enough to earn a second star but based on NYE 2011, I wouldn't in good conscience recommend it to my worst enemy. The blame must lie squarely on poor management. Period. Remember, you KNEW AHEAD OF TIME you were FULLY BOOKED for NYE. I was ready to write the BBB, the CEO of Choice Hotels International, my Congressman and the Mayor but figured this review would suffice...for now.

I thought, "Hey that's a pretty good deal" since we were also getting the VIP room. After talking to him some more I asked for a comp for the guys that paid for my table. Up to this point he was extremely helpful. He waved the fee for 5 guys and I told him I would just pay for the other 5 making my tab total $225 since its $10 for each guy. So I sent him a list of my ten guys I wanted to get into the place for free and thought that was all I needed. He neglected to tell me that per bottle there was a 15 person max.
